document.title: K-12 Mathematics New Hampshire Curriculum Framework

BBD127B0DFE60131771168A86D17958E.description:
Students will recognize, explore, and develop mathematical connections and be able to:
  • See mathematics as an integrated whole.
  • Recognize relationships among different topics in mathematics.
  • Recognize and use mathematics in other curriculum areas and in their daily lives.
  • Link concepts and procedures.
  • Use mathematical skills, concepts, and applications in other disciplines (e.g., graphs in social studies, patterns in art, or music and geometry in technology education).

BBD0DA80DFE60131771068A86D17958E.description:
Students will create and use representations to communicate mathematical ideas and to solve problems and be able to:
  • Use physical models and diagrams to represent important mathematical ideas (e.g., multiplication).
  • Use appropriate representations to solve problems or to portray, clarify, or extend a mathematical idea.
  • Recognize equivalent representations of concepts and procedures and translate among them as appropriate (for example, understand how the addition of whole numbers, fractions, and decimals are related).

BBD08B00DFE60131770F68A86D17958E.description:
Students will communicate their understanding of mathematics and be able to:
  • Discuss mathematical ideas and write convincing arguments.
  • Understand, explain, analyze, and evaluate mathematical arguments and conclusions presented by others.
  • Ask clarifying and extending questions related to mathematics they have heard or read about.
  • Understand and appreciate the economy and power of mathematical symbolism and its role in the development of mathematics.
  • Demonstrate an understanding of mathematical concepts and relationships through a variety of methods (e.g., writing, graphing, charts, diagrams, number sentences, or symbols).
  • Use a variety of technologies (e.g., computers, calculators, video, probes) to represent and communicate mathematical ideas.

BBD00AE0DFE60131770D68A86D17958E.description:
Students will use mathematical reasoning and proof and be able to:
  • Draw conclusions and solve problems using elementary deductive reasoning and reasoning by analogy.
  • Make and defend conjectures and generalizations.
  • Use models, known facts, properties, and relationships to explain thinking and to justify answers and solution processes.
  • Recognize the pervasive use and power of reasoning as a part of mathematics.

BBCFC3E0DFE60131770C68A86D17958E.description:
Students will use problem-solving strategies to investigate and understand increasingly complex mathematical content and be able to:
  • Determine the reasonableness of solutions to real-world problems.
  • Generalize solutions and apply strategies to new problem situations.
  • Add to the repertoire of problem-solving strategies (e.g., looking for similar problems) and use those strategies in more sophisticated ways.
  • Solve problems with multiple solutions, recognize when a problem has no solution, and recognize problems where more information is needed.
  • Translate results of a computation into solutions that fit the real-world problem (e.g., when a computation shows that one needs 3.2 gallons of paint to paint a room, how much paint do you buy?).

BBCF3110DFE60131770A68A86D17958E.description: In response to a teacher or student generated question or hypothesis decides the most effective method (e.g., survey, observation, experimentation) to collect the data (numerical or categorical) necessary to answer the question; collects, organizes, and appropriately displays the data; analyzes the data to draw conclusions about the question or hypothesis being tested, and when appropriate makes predictions; and asks new questions and makes connections to real world situations.

BBCEE4B0DFE60131770968A86D17958E.description: For a probability event in which the sample space may or may not contain equally likely outcomes, determines the experimental or theoretical probability of an event and expresses the result as a fraction.

BBCEA2B0DFE60131770868A86D17958E.description: For a probability event in which the sample space may or may not contain equally likely outcomes, predicts the likelihood of an event as a fraction and tests the prediction through experiments; and determines if a game is fair.

BBCE5B70DFE60131770768A86D17958E.description: Identifies or describes representations or elements of representations that best display a given set of data or situation, consistent with the representations required in M:DSP:5:1.

BBCE13D0DFE60131770668A86D17958E.description: Organizes and displays data using tables, bar graphs, or line graphs to answer questions related to the data, to analyze the data to formulate or justify conclusions, to make predictions, or to solve problems.

BBCDCAE0DFE60131770568A86D17958E.description: Analyzes patterns, trends, or distributions in data in a variety of contexts by determining or using measures of central tendency (mean, median, or mode) or range to analyze situations, or to solve problems.

BBCD76F0DFE60131770468A86D17958E.description: Interprets a given representation (tables, bar graphs, circle graphs, or line graphs) to answer questions related to the data, to analyze the data to formulate or justify conclusions, to make predictions, or to solve problems.

BBCCB5F0DFE60131770268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates conceptual understanding of equality by showing equivalence between two expressions using models or different representations of the expressions (expressions consistent with the parameters of M:F&A:5–3), by solving one-step linear equations of the form ax = c, x ± b = c, or x/a = c, where a, b, and c are whole numbers with a ≠ 0; or by determining which values of a replacement set make the equation (multi-step of the form ax ± b = c where a, b, and c are whole numbers with a ≠ 0) a true statement (e.g., 2x + 3 = 11, {x: x = 2, 3, 4, 5}).

BBCC7180DFE60131770168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates conceptual understanding of algebraic expressions by using letters to represent unknown quantities to write linear algebraic expressions involving any two of the four operations; or by evaluating linear algebraic expressions using whole numbers.

BBCC19D0DFE60131770068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates conceptual understanding of linear relationships (y = kx) as a constant rate of change by identifying, describing, or comparing situations that represent constant rates of change (e.g., tell a story given a line graph about a trip).

BBCB98C0DFE6013176FF68A86D17958E.description: Identifies and extends to specific cases a variety of patterns (linear and nonlinear) represented in models, tables, sequences, or in problem situations; and writes a rule in words or symbols for finding specific cases of a linear relationship.

BBCB0FE0DFE6013176FD68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates conceptual understanding of spatial reasoning and visualization by building models of rectangular and triangular prisms, cones, cylinders, and pyramids from two- or three-dimensional representations.

BBCACC50DFE6013176FC68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates understanding of spatial relationships using location and position by interpreting and giving directions between locations on a map or coordinate grid (all four quadrants); plotting points in four quadrants in context (e.g., games, mapping, identifying the vertices of polygons as they are reflected, rotated, and translated); and determining horizontal and vertical distances between points on a coordinate grid in the first quadrant.

BBCA89A0DFE6013176FB68A86D17958E.description: Measures and uses units of measures appropriately and consistently, and makes conversions within systems when solving problems across the content strands.

BBCA4290DFE6013176FA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates conceptual understanding of perimeter of polygons, and the area of rectangles or right triangles through models, manipulatives, or formulas, the area of polygons or irregular figures on grids, and volume of rectangular prisms (cubes) using a variety of models, manipulatives, or formulas. Expresses all measures using appropriate units.

BBC9F7A0DFE6013176F968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates conceptual understanding of similarity by describing the proportional effect on the linear dimensions of triangles and rectangles when scaling up or down while preserving angle measures, or by solving related problems (including applying scales on maps). Describes effects using models or explanations.

BBC9B0E0DFE6013176F868A86D17958E.description: Uses properties or attributes (shape of bases, number of lateral faces, or number of bases) to identify, compare, or describe three-dimensional shapes (rectangular prisms, triangular prisms, cylinders, spheres, pyramids, or cones).

BBC96ED0DFE6013176F768A86D17958E.description: Uses properties or attributes of angles (right, acute, or obtuse) or sides (number of congruent sides, parallelism, or perpendicularity) to identify, describe, classify, or distinguish among different types of triangles (right, acute, obtuse, equiangular, or equilateral) or quadrilaterals (rectangles, squares, rhombi, trapezoids, or parallelograms).

BBC8EDE0DFE6013176F568A86D17958E.description: Applies properties of numbers (odd, even, and divisibility) and field properties (commutative, associative, identity, and distributive) to solve problems and to simplify computations.

BBC8A810DFE6013176F468A86D17958E.description: Makes estimates in a given situation by identifying when estimation is appropriate, selecting the appropriate method of estimation, determining the level of accuracy needed given the situation, analyzing the effect of the estimation method on the accuracy of results, and evaluating the reasonableness of solutions appropriate to grade level GLEs across content strands.

BBC85B00DFE6013176F368A86D17958E.description: Mentally calculates change back from $1.00, $5.00, and $10.00; calculates multiplication and related division facts to a product of 144; multiplies a two-digit whole number by a one-digit whole number (e.g., 45 × 5), two-digit whole numbers that are multiples of ten (e.g., 50 × 60), a three-digit whole number that is a multiple of 100 by a two- or three-digit number which is a multiple of 10 or 100, respectively (e.g., 400 × 50, 400 × 600); and divides 3- and 4-digit multiples of powers of ten by their compatible factors (e.g., 360 ÷ 6; 360 ÷ 60; 3600 ÷ 6; 3600 ÷ 60; 3600 ÷ 600; 360 ÷ 12; 360 ÷ 120; 3600 ÷ 12; 3600 ÷ 120; 3600 ÷ 1200).

BBC80CB0DFE6013176F268A86D17958E.description: Accurately solves problems involving multiple operations on whole numbers or the use of the properties of factors, multiples, prime, or composite numbers; and addition or subtraction of fractions (proper) and decimals to the hundredths place. (Division of whole numbers by up to a twodigit divisor.)

BBC7C210DFE6013176F168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates conceptual understanding of mathematical operations by describing or illustrating the meaning of a remainder with respect to division of whole numbers using models, explanations, or solving problems.

BBC77770DFE6013176F068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates conceptual understanding of mathematical operations by adding and subtracting decimals and positive proper fractions with unlike denominators.

BBC73030DFE6013176EF68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates understanding of the relative magnitude of numbers by ordering, comparing, or identifying equivalent positive fractional numbers, decimals, or benchmark percents within number formats (fractions to fractions, decimals to decimals, or percents to percents); or integers in context using models or number lines.

BBC6E3C0DFE6013176EE68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrates conceptual understanding of rational numbers with respect to: whole numbers from 0 to 9,999,999 through equivalency, composition, decomposition, or place value using models, explanations, or other representations; and positive fractional numbers (proper, mixed number, and improper) (halves, fourths, eighths, thirds, sixths, twelfths, fifths, or powers of ten (10, 100, 1000)), decimals (to thousandths), or benchmark percents (10%, 25%, 50%, 75% or 100%) as a part to whole relationship in area, set, or linear models using models, explanations, or other representations.

document.title: K-12 Social Studies New Hampshire Curriculum Framework

B9D5A670DFE6013173DE68A86D17958E.description: Describe different ways that societies around the world express their values and beliefs through practices, e.g., festivals or dress. (Themes: B: Civic Ideals, Practices, and Engagement, E: Cultural Development, Interaction, and Change, I: Patterns of Social and Political Interaction)

B9D55B70DFE6013173DD68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate their understanding of the diversity of values, beliefs, and practices of individuals and groups over time.

B9D487E0DFE6013173DB68A86D17958E.description: Explore how improvements in agriculture enhance human survival using examples, e.g., the exchange between Native Americans and early colonists or feeding the hungry of the world today. (Themes: F: Global Transformation, G: Science, Technology, and Society)

B9D42E70DFE6013173DA68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate their understanding of the changing forms of production, distribution and consumption of goods and services over time.

B9D39D00DFE6013173D868A86D17958E.description: Describe ways that societies around the world express themselves artistically through forms, e.g., architecture or folk tales. (Themes: J: Human Expression and Communication)

B9D350B0DFE6013173D768A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate their understanding of conceptions of reality, ideals, guidelines of behavior and their forms of expression.

B9D302D0DFE6013173D668A86D17958E.description: World Views and Value systems and their Intellectual and Artistic Expressions

B9D2AAB0DFE6013173D568A86D17958E.description: Explain how events or global issues affect interactions between countries, e.g., the Olympics or the war on terrorism. (Themes: B: Civic Ideals, Practices, and Engagement, F: Global Transformation, G: Science, Technology, and Society)

B9D26450DFE6013173D468A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate their understanding of the interactions of peoples and governments over time.

B9D1D5E0DFE6013173D268A86D17958E.description: Explain that people of different countries create social and political systems, e.g., a family or a government. (Themes: A: Conflict and Cooperation, B: Civic Ideals, Practices, and Engagement, I: Patterns of Social and Political Interaction)

B9D18CF0DFE6013173D168A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of major events, ideas and issues pertaining to the history of governance.

B9D09B00DFE6013173CE68A86D17958E.description: Describe the reasons why various groups have come to the United States, e.g., enslavement or economic opportunity. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, F: Global Transformation, H: Individualism, Equality and Authority)

B9D04D30DFE6013173CD68A86D17958E.description: Explore attitudes towards diversity, e.g., segregation or inclusion. (Themes: E: Cultural Development, Interaction, and Change, I: Patterns of Social and Political Interaction)

B9CFFE30DFE6013173CC68A86D17958E.description: Trace the changes in the roles and lives of women and children and their impact on society, e.g., the family or the workplace. (Themes: B: Civic Ideals, Practices, and Engagement, I: Patterns of Social and Political Interaction)

B9CF8880DFE6013173CB68A86D17958E.description: Describe the impact of major national and state events on everyday life, e.g., the American Revolution or the terrorist attacks on 9.11.2001. (Themes: B: Civic Ideals, Practices, and Engagement, I: Patterns of Social and Political Interaction)

B9C8CD90DFE6013173CA68A86D17958E.description: Explain the unique contributions of different ethnic and religious groups to New Hampshire history and culture, e.g., the Shakers or the French Canadians. (Themes: E: Cultural Development, Interaction, and Change, I: Patterns of Social and Political Interaction, J: Human Expression and Communication)

B9C86D70DFE6013173C968A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the interaction of various social groups, including their values, beliefs and practices, over time.

B9C7C210DFE6013173C768A86D17958E.description: Investigate the evolution of the United States economy, e.g., the transition from farms to factories or the trend from small local stores to shopping malls. (Themes: D: Material Wants and Needs, G: Science, Technology, and Society)

B9C768D0DFE6013173C668A86D17958E.description: Explore the impact of important technological inventions, e.g., new forms of transportation or housing. (Themes: E: Cultural Development, Interaction, and Change, G: Science, Technology, and Society)

B9C70B60DFE6013173C568A86D17958E.description: Explore major developments and changes in economic productivity, e.g., adoption of Native American crops or use of mass production. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, F: Global Transformation, G: Science, Technology, and Society)

B9C6A580DFE6013173C468A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the changing forms of production, distribution and consumption of goods and services over time.

B9C5FE80DFE6013173C268A86D17958E.description: Explore how groups have enhanced the art, music and literature of our nation, e.g., Latinos or Franco Americans. (Themes: E: Cultural Development, Interaction, and Change, F: Global Transformation, J: Human Expression and Communication)

B9C5B100DFE6013173C168A86D17958E.description: Explore how art, music and literature often reflect and/or influence major ideas, values and conflicts of particular time periods, e.g., colonial life or industrialization in New Hampshire. (Themes: J: Human Expression and Communication)

B9C56180DFE6013173C068A86D17958E.description: Explore how individuals' ideals have profoundly affected life in the United States, e.g., Martin Luther King Jr.'s belief in nonviolence or John Stark's statement "Live Free or Die". (Themes: H: Individualism, Equality and Authority, I: Patterns of Social and Political Interaction, J: Human Expression and Communication)

B9C50F80DFE6013173BF68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of conceptions of reality, ideals, guidelines of behavior and forms of expression.

B9C4BC50DFE6013173BE68A86D17958E.description: World Views and Value systems and their Intellectual and Artistic Expressions

B9C45240DFE6013173BD68A86D17958E.description: Describe the interconnectedness of the world developed using examples., e.g., the contact between Native Americans and European settlers or the location of family members serving in foreign countries. (Themes: A: Conflict and Cooperation, C: People, Places and Environment, D: Material Wants and Needs)

B9C3D7E0DFE6013173BC68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the events, actions and policies of our nation in relation to other peoples and governments over time.

B9C33680DFE6013173BA68A86D17958E.description: Describe the significance of national and New Hampshire celebrations, monuments, symbols and documents, e.g., Veteran's Day, the Statue of Liberty, Old Man of the Mountain, and the preamble to the New Hampshire Constitution. (Themes: B: Civic Ideals, Practices, and Engagement, C: People, Places and Environment)

B9C2E5B0DFE6013173B968A86D17958E.description: Trace the political development of New Hampshire governance, e.g., self-government in early settlements or the development of current forms of local government. (Themes: A: Conflict and Cooperation)

B9C28D10DFE6013173B868A86D17958E.description: Explore biographies of key political figures who helped shape our community, state, and country, e.g., Franklin Pierce or Sandra Day O'Connor. (Themes: E: Cultural Development, Interaction, and Change, G: Science, Technology, and Society, I: Patterns of Social and Political Interaction)

B9C23D40DFE6013173B768A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the major ideas, issues and events pertaining to the history of governance in our state and nation.

B9C13EB0DFE6013173B468A86D17958E.description: Compare how people in different regions use the same resource, e.g., water or wood.(Themes: D: Material Wants and Needs, G: Science, Technology, and Society)

B9C0E8A0DFE6013173B368A86D17958E.description: Describe the role of natural resources in daily life, e.g., food, clothing, or shelter. (Themes: D: Material Wants and Needs)

B9C09770DFE6013173B268A86D17958E.description: Examine the effects of the use of renewable and nonrenewable resources on human systems, e.g., climate change or fluctuating oil prices. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, D: Material Wants and Needs)

B9C03430DFE6013173B168A86D17958E.description: Examine the ways in which the physical environment provides opportunities or limitations, e.g., natural resources that first attracted settlers or natural hazards that threaten life. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, D: Material Wants and Needs)

B9BFD710DFE6013173B068A86D17958E.description: Illustrate how people modify the physical environment, e.g., irrigation projects or clearing land for human use. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, D: Material Wants and Needs)

B9BF7DC0DFE6013173AF68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the connections and consequences of the interactions between Earth's physical and human systems.

B9BECA80DFE6013173AD68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the spatial patterns of settlement in different regions of the world, e.g., urbanization along rivers or nomadic movement patterns. (Themes: E: Cultural Development, Interaction, and Change, I: Patterns of Social and Political Interaction)

B9BE5B00DFE6013173AC68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the effects of migration on the characteristics of places, e.g., cultural awareness or food choices. (Themes: E: Cultural Development, Interaction, and Change)

B9BDF230DFE6013173AB68A86D17958E.description: Describe the types and historical patterns of human migration, e.g., chain migration or slave trade. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, I: Patterns of Social and Political Interaction)

B9BD9BA0DFE6013173AA68A86D17958E.description: Recognize the distribution of a population and its underlying causes, e.g., rural, suburban or urban. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, I: Patterns of Social and Political Interaction)

B9BD3C50DFE6013173A968A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of human migration; the complexity of cultural mosaics; economic interdependence; human settlement patterns; and the forces of cooperation and conflict among peoples.

B9BCA3B0DFE6013173A768A86D17958E.description: Investigate how humans interact with ecosystems, e.g., forest management or impacting wetlands. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, D: Material Wants and Needs, F: Global Transformation)

B9BC5A60DFE6013173A668A86D17958E.description: Recognize the components and distribution of ecosystems, e.g., the location of certain plants and animals or the food chain. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment)

B9BC1040DFE6013173A568A86D17958E.description: Describe how the Earth-Sun relationship affects conditions on Earth, e.g., seasons at different locations on Earth, length of daylight. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment)

B9BBC360DFE6013173A468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how physical processes shape features of Earth's surface, e.g., weather or tectonic forces. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment)

B9BB5E80DFE6013173A368A86D17958E.description: Illustrate the components of Earth's physical systems, e.g., a climate or a model of the water cycle. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment)

B9BB1180DFE6013173A268A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the physical processes that shape the patterns of Earth's surface and the characteristics and spatial distribution of ecosystems.

B9BA63B0DFE6013173A068A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the ways in which different people perceive places, e.g., drawings and sketch maps of familiar places or examples from children's literature. (Themes: J: Human Expression and Communication)

B9BA0AA0DFE60131739F68A86D17958E.description: Illustrate the ways in which regions change, e.g., changes in local neighborhoods or changes to the United States through westward expansion. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, E: Cultural Development, Interaction, and Change, I: Patterns of Social and Political Interaction

B9B9BBF0DFE60131739E68A86D17958E.description: Generalize the concept of region as an area of Earth's surface with unifying geographic characteristics, e.g., neighborhoods or climate regions. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment)

B9B962D0DFE60131739D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize how physical and human processes together shape places, e.g., the relationship between elevation and population density in a region or the characteristics of regions along the same latitude. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment)

B9B90F80DFE60131739C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the physical and human characteristics of places, e.g., land forms or where people live. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, E: Cultural Development, Interaction, and Change, G: Science, Technology, and Society)

B9B8A470DFE60131739B68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the physical and human geographic features that define places and regions as well as how culture and experience influence people's perceptions of places and regions.

B9B7F430DFE60131739968A86D17958E.description: Recognize the causes and consequences of spatial interaction on Earth's surface, e.g., the origin of consumer goods or transportation routes. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, D: Material Wants and Needs, F: Global Transformation)

B9B79910DFE60131739868A86D17958E.description: Illustrate that places and features are distributed spatially across Earth's surface, e.g., community grid maps or population density maps. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, F: Global Transformation, I: Patterns of Social and Political Interaction)

B9B74EF0DFE60131739768A86D17958E.description: Locate major physical and human features in the United States and on Earth, e.g., mountain ranges, principal parallels or meridians. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, G: Science, Technology, and Society)

B9B702C0DFE60131739668A86D17958E.description: Display spatial information on maps and other geographic representations, e.g., home-to-school routes or settings in appropriate children's literature. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, G: Science, Technology, and Society, J: Human Expression and Communication)

B9B6B730DFE60131739568A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the characteristics and purposes of geographic tools: maps, globes, graphs, diagrams, photographs, satellite-produced images, and other technologies. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, F: Global Transformation)

B9B669F0DFE60131739468A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate the ability to use maps, mental maps, globes, and other graphic tools and technologies to acquire, process, report, and analyze geographic information.

B9B55850DFE60131739168A86D17958E.description: Explain that trade between countries involves imports and exports and the reasons why countries trade. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, D: Material Wants and Needs, F: Global Transformation)

B9B4FBA0DFE60131739068A86D17958E.description: Explain why some countries' resources are in greater demand than others, e.g., colonial New Hampshire's mast trees or petroleum. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, D: Material Wants and Needs, F: Global Transformation)

B9B4AE80DFE60131738F68A86D17958E.description: Describe that countries have different kinds of resources. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, D: Material Wants and Needs

B9B45D20DFE60131738E68A86D17958E.description: Students will recognize the importance of international trade and how economies are affected by it.

B9B3B370DFE60131738C68A86D17958E.description: Identify good and services provided by local government, e.g., police cars or fire protection. (Themes: A: Conflict and Cooperation, C: People, Places and Environment, G: Science, Technology, and Society)

B9B35F80DFE60131738B68A86D17958E.description: escribe different methods people use to exchange goods and services, e.g., barter or the use of money. (Themes: D: Material Wants and Needs)

B9B2EE10DFE60131738A68A86D17958E.description: Students will understand how financial institutions and the government work together to stabilize our economy, and how changes in them affect the individual.

B9B22EA0DFE60131738868A86D17958E.description: Describe how changes in the business cycle can impact people's lives. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment)

B9B1E1F0DFE60131738768A86D17958E.description: Illustrate cycles of economic growth and decline, e.g., New Hampshire manufacturing or agriculture. (Themes: D: Material Wants and Needs, F: Global Transformation, G: Science, Technology, and Society)

B9B194D0DFE60131738668A86D17958E.description: Students will be able to explain the business cycle and trends in economic activity over time.

B9B0F8E0DFE60131738468A86D17958E.description: Explain how prices of goods and services are set in the United States and describe different factors that affect price. (Themes: D: Material Wants and Needs, F: Global Transformation)

B9B0A010DFE60131738368A86D17958E.description: Define supply and demand and describe factors that can cause a change in supply and demand. (Themes: D: Material Wants and Needs, F: Global Transformation)

B9B03DA0DFE60131738268A86D17958E.description: Describe different ways individuals, households, businesses and governments make economic decisions, e.g., developing alternative choices or budgets. (Themes: A: Conflict and Cooperation, D: Material Wants and Needs, G: Science, Technology, and Society)

B9AFE160DFE60131738168A86D17958E.description: Explain why scarcity requires individuals, households, businesses and governments to make economic choices and how economic choices always involve an opportunity cost. (Themes: A: Conflict and Cooperation, D: Material Wants and Needs)

B9AF96A0DFE60131738068A86D17958E.description: Explain why needs and wants are unlimited while resources are limited. (Themes: C: People, Places and Environment, D: Material Wants and Needs)

B9AF38C0DFE60131737F68A86D17958E.description: Students will learn about the pillars of a free market economy and the market mechanism.

B9AE8860DFE60131737D68A86D17958E.description: Describe why most jobs today require greater specialization and result in greater productivity. (Themes: G: Science, Technology, and Society)

B9AE3840DFE60131737C68A86D17958E.description: Explain how decisions by consumers and producers affect and are affected by the economy. (Themes A: Conflict and Cooperation C: People, Places and Environment D: Material Wants and Needs)

B9ADEA50DFE60131737B68A86D17958E.description: Describe what markets are and define individual's roles as consumers and producers in a market economy using circular flow models. (Themes: D: Material Wants and Needs, G: Science, Technology, and Society)

B9AD9580DFE60131737A68A86D17958E.description: Identify the factors of production and explain how businesses use these to produce goods and services. (Themes: D: Material Wants and Needs, G: Science, Technology, and Society)

B9AD3660DFE60131737968A86D17958E.description: Students will learn about their role in a free market, how decisions that they make affect the economy, and how changes in the economy can affect them.

B9AC3FA0DFE60131737668A86D17958E.description: Describe the rights of citizens as outlined by the Constitutions of New Hampshire and the United States. (Themes: A: Conflict and Cooperation, H: Individualism, Equality and Authority)

B9ABF740DFE60131737568A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the rights and responsibilities of citizenship, and the ability to apply their knowledge of local, state, and national government through the political process and citizen involvement.

B9AB6010DFE60131737368A86D17958E.description: Explain that the world is divided into different countries with their own governments and that all governments are not the same. (Themes: A: Conflict and Cooperation, E: Cultural Development, Interaction, and Change, I: Patterns of Social and Political Interaction)

B9AB0D10DFE60131737268A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the relationship of the United States to other countries, and the role of the United States in world affairs.

B9AAC490DFE60131737168A86D17958E.description: The World and the United States' Place In It

B9AA7A60DFE60131737068A86D17958E.description: Explain how laws and/or policies are made at local and state levels. (Themes: A: Conflict and Cooperation, B: Civic Ideals, Practices, and Engagement, H: Individualism, Equality and Authority)

B9AA3240DFE60131736F68A86D17958E.description: Identify the individual functions of the three branches of government and the organization of New Hampshire state government. (Themes: A: Conflict and Cooperation, B: Civic Ideals, Practices, and Engagement)

B9A9E850DFE60131736E68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of major provisions of the United States and New Hampshire Constitutions, and the organization and operation of government at all levels including the legislative, executive, and judicial branches.

B9A99A90DFE60131736D68A86D17958E.description: Structure and Function of United States and New Hampshire Government

B9A941E0DFE60131736C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze how government addresses social, political, and geographic issues. e.g., local land use decisions or decisions involving human rights. (Themes: 1: Conflict and Cooperation, B: Civic Ideals, Practices, and Engagement, C: People, Places and Environment)

B9A8E6A0DFE60131736B68A86D17958E.description: Explain the ideal of the United States system of government, e.g., equal rights or tolerance for others. (Themes: A: Conflict and Cooperation, B: Civic Ideals, Practices, and Engagement, C: People, Places and Environment)

B9A89420DFE60131736A68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the nature of governments, and the fundamental ideals of government of the United States.

B9A83D40DFE60131736968A86D17958E.description: The Nature and Purpose of Government

B9E90920DFE60131741A68A86D17958E.description: Participate in community projects such as voter registration, blood drives, conservation, and heritage activities

B9E8B470DFE60131741968A86D17958E.description: Accept and fulfill responsibilities associated with citizenship in a free society

B9E85F70DFE60131741868A86D17958E.description: Work to influence those in leadership positions to strive for extensions of freedom, justice, and human rights

B9E807C0DFE60131741768A86D17958E.description: Work individually or with others to decide on an appropriate course of action

B9E7B9C0DFE60131741668A86D17958E.description: Identify situations in which civic action is required

B9E76930DFE60131741568A86D17958E.description: Keep informed on issues that affect society

B9E70F20DFE60131741468A86D17958E.description: Students will develop civic participation skills:

B9E6C0F0DFE60131741368A86D17958E.description: Participate in persuading, compromising, debating, and negotiating the resolution of conflicts and differences

B9E66DF0DFE60131741268A86D17958E.description: Appropriately adjust one's own behavior in response to the dynamics of various groups and situations

B9E61160DFE60131741168A86D17958E.description: Communicate and defend one's own belief, feelings, and convictions

B9E4B2B0DFE60131740D68A86D17958E.description: Take into account relevant ethical values and principles

B9E467C0DFE60131740C68A86D17958E.description: Identify alternative courses of action and predict likely consequences of each

B9E419F0DFE60131740B68A86D17958E.description: Secure needed factual information relevant to making the decision

B9E3B810DFE60131740A68A86D17958E.description: Students will be make informed decisions:

B9E2D4B0DFE60131740868A86D17958E.description: Present orally (presentation, debate, group discussion, simulation, etc.)

B9D83100DFE6013173E668A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between primary and secondary sources.

B9D7E4C0DFE6013173E568A86D17958E.description: Students will be able to comprehend the wide range of social studies-related materials by using skills:

B9D796F0DFE6013173E468A86D17958E.description: Draw on the diversity of social studies-related sources, such as auditory and visual sources, such as documents, charts, pictures, architectural works, and music.

B9D74870DFE6013173E368A86D17958E.description: Discriminate to select the most worthwhile and trustworthy sources

B9D6EF30DFE6013173E268A86D17958E.description: Use economic and geographic data, historical sources, as well as other appropriate sources

document.title: K-12 Science Literacy New Hampshire Curriculum Framework

B5D43870DFE601316C4E68A86D17958E.description: Understand that some form of science is used in most jobs/careers and that some jobs/careers specifically require knowledge of physical science.

B5D37770DFE601316C4C68A86D17958E.description: Provide an example to show that manufacturing processes involve changing natural materials into finished products through a series of processes that involve physical and/or chemical changes.

B5D31520DFE601316C4B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how to produce a magnetic force with an electric current, such as an electromagnet, and how to produce an electric current with a magnet, such as a generator.

B5D2AFA0DFE601316C4A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how a battery changes chemical energy into electrical energy.

B5D233D0DFE601316C4968A86D17958E.description: Social Issues (Local and Global) Energy, Power, and Transportation Manufacturing

B5D1DA80DFE601316C4868A86D17958E.description: Recognize that manufacturing processes use a variety of tools and machines to separate, form, combine and condition natural and synthetic materials.

B5D134D0DFE601316C4668A86D17958E.description: Understand that scientific principles are used in the design of technology.

B5D08100DFE601316C4468A86D17958E.description: The growth of scientific knowledge in Physical Science has been advanced through the development of technology and is used (alone or in combination with other sciences) to identify, understand and solve local and global issues.

B5D01730DFE601316C4368A86D17958E.description: Explain that an object's motion can be tracked and measured over time and that the data can be used to describe its position.

B5CFBE10DFE601316C4268A86D17958E.description: Explain the how balanced and unbalanced forces are related to an object's motion.

B5CF0B10DFE601316C4068A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationship between the strength of a force on an object and the resulting effect, such as the greater the force, the greater the change in motion.

B5CEADA0DFE601316C3F68A86D17958E.description: Explain that when a force is applied to an object, it reacts in one of three ways: the object either speeds up, slows down, or goes in a different direction.

B5CE42E0DFE601316C3E68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that just as electric currents can produce magnetic forces, magnets can cause electric currents.

B5CD83B0DFE601316C3C68A86D17958E.description: The motion of an object is affected by force.

B5CD2790DFE601316C3B68A86D17958E.description: Explain how electrical circuits can be used to transfer energy in order to produce heat, light, sound, and chemical changes.

B5CCCF90DFE601316C3A68A86D17958E.description: Explain that heat energy moves from warmer materials or regions to cooler ones through conduction, convection, and radiation.

B5CC77F0DFE601316C3968A86D17958E.description: Recognize that energy, in the form of heat, is usually a by-product when one form of energy is changed to another, such as when machines convert stored energy to motion.

B5CC2610DFE601316C3868A86D17958E.description: Explain that sound vibrations move at different speeds, have different wavelengths; and establish wave-like disturbances that emanate from the source.

B5CBD0C0DFE601316C3768A86D17958E.description: Explain that the pitch of a sound is dependent on the frequency of the vibration producing it.

B5CB1E20DFE601316C3568A86D17958E.description: Describe how mass remains constant in a closed system and provide examples relating to both physical and chemical change.

B5CA5780DFE601316C3368A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between a physical change, such as melting, and a chemical change, such as rusting.

B5C9B2E0DFE601316C3168A86D17958E.description: Energy is necessary for change to occur in matter. Energy can be stored, transferred and transformed, but cannot be destroyed.

B5C95E10DFE601316C3068A86D17958E.description: Identify energy as a property of many substances.

B5C8ADB0DFE601316C2E68A86D17958E.description: Identify substances by their physical and chemical properties, such as magnetism, conductivity, density, solubility, boiling and melting points.

B5C858A0DFE601316C2D68A86D17958E.description: Identify elements according to their common properties, such as highly reactive metals, less reactive metals, highly reactive non-metals and almost non-reactive gases.

B5C7AE70DFE601316C2B68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that over one hundred elements exist, and identify the periodic table as a tool for organizing the information about them.

B5C74770DFE601316C2A68A86D17958E.description: Identify elements as substances that contain only one kind of atom; and explain that elements do not break down by normal laboratory reactions, such as heating, exposure to electric current, and reaction to acid.

B5C6EF50DFE601316C2968A86D17958E.description: Recognize that all matter is composed of minute particles called atoms; and explain that all substances are composed of atoms, each arranged into different groupings.

B5C62C00DFE601316C2768A86D17958E.description: All living and nonliving things are composed of matter having characteristic properties that distinguish one substance from another (independent of size/amount of substance).

B5C55F40DFE601316C2568A86D17958E.description: Understand that some form of science is used in most jobs/careers and that some jobs/careers specifically require knowledge of life science.

B5C4A9F0DFE601316C2368A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe some of the processes and systems used to grow food in New Hampshire, including irrigation, pest control and harvesting.

B5C45640DFE601316C2268A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the quality of personal health can be influenced by society and technology.

B5C3FEA0DFE601316C2168A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between vaccines, which help prevent diseases from developing and spreading, and medicines, which relieve symptoms or cure diseases.

B5C3A580DFE601316C2068A86D17958E.description: Provide examples of early health care technology that helped to extend the life expectancy of humans, such as the discovery of penicillin and sterilization of surgical instruments.

B5C352A0DFE601316C1F68A86D17958E.description: Social Issues (Local And Global) Medical Technology and Biotechnology

B5C300D0DFE601316C1E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the appropriate use of tools, such as thermometers, probes, microscopes and computers to gather, analyze and interpret data in the life sciences.

B5C25880DFE601316C1C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that an agricultural system is designed to maximize the use of all the elements in the system, including using plants for food, oxygen, for the filtration of air and water, and for making compost.

B5C1A920DFE601316C1A68A86D17958E.description: The growth of scientific knowledge in Life Science has been advanced through the development of technology and is used (alone or in combination with other sciences) to identify, understand and solve local and global issues.

B5C14CB0DFE601316C1968A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the length and quality of human life are influenced by many factors, including sanitation, diet, medical care, gender, genes, environmental conditions, and personal health behaviors.

B5C085E0DFE601316C1768A86D17958E.description: Recognize a healthy body cannot fight all germs that invade it; and explain how some germs interfere with the body's defenses.

B5C028B0DFE601316C1668A86D17958E.description: Explain how vaccines induce the body to build immunity to a disease without actually causing the disease itself.

B5BFD2F0DFE601316C1568A86D17958E.description: Recognize that there are some diseases that human beings can only get once; and explain how many diseases can be prevented by vaccination.

B5BF78E0DFE601316C1468A86D17958E.description: Explain that the human body has ways to defend itself against disease-causing organisms and describe how defenders, including tears, saliva, the skin, some blood cells and stomach secretions support the defense process.

B5BE92C0DFE601316C1268A86D17958E.description: Provide examples of how humans make judgments about new situations based on memories of past experiences.

B5BE3610DFE601316C1168A86D17958E.description: Explain that people can learn about others from direct experience, from the media, and from listening to others talk about their life and work.

B5BDE1C0DFE601316C1068A86D17958E.description: Recognize that learning requires more than just storage and retrieval of information and that prior knowledge needs to be tapped in order to make sense out of new experiences or information.

B5BD38E0DFE601316C0E68A86D17958E.description: Humans are similar to other species in many ways, and yet are unique among Earth's life forms.

B5B807C0DFE601316C0068A86D17958E.description: Recognize that only organisms that are able to reproduce can pass on their genetic information to the next generation.

B5B7ABE0DFE601316BFF68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that there are genetic variations among individuals in groups of organisms and provide examples of how these variations affect the survival of an organism.

B5B6D700DFE601316BFD68A86D17958E.description: Describe the fundamental concepts related to biological evolution, such as biological adaptations and the diversity of species.

B5B623F0DFE601316BFB68A86D17958E.description: Explain how changes in environmental conditions can affect the survival of individual organisms and the entire species.

B5B5D180DFE601316BFA68A86D17958E.description: Provide examples of how all organisms, including humans, impact their environment; and explain how some changes can be detrimental to other organisms.

B5B52160DFE601316BF868A86D17958E.description: Groups of organisms show evidence of change over time (e.g. evolution, natural selection, structures, behaviors, and biochemistry).

B5BCDD40DFE601316C0D68A86D17958E.description: Explain how insects and various other organisms depend on dead plant and animal matter for food; and describe how this process contributes to the system.

B5BC72A0DFE601316C0C68A86D17958E.description: Using food webs, identify and describe the ways in which organisms interact and depend on one another in an ecosystem.

B5BC13B0DFE601316C0B68A86D17958E.description: Define a population as all individuals of a species that exist together at a given place and time; and explain that all populations living together in a community, along with the physical factors with which they interact, compose an ecosystem.

B5BB5610DFE601316C0968A86D17958E.description: Recognize that energy, in the form of heat, is usually a byproduct when one form of energy is converted to another, such as when living organisms transform stored energy to motion.

B5BB0160DFE601316C0868A86D17958E.description: Describe the process of photosynthesis and explain that plants can use the food they make immediately or store it for later use.

B5BAA740DFE601316C0768A86D17958E.description: Recognize that one of the most general distinctions among organisms is between plants, which use sunlight to make their own food, and animals, which consume energy-rich foods.

B5BA5180DFE601316C0668A86D17958E.description: Describe how energy is transferred in an ecosystem through food webs; and explain the roles and relationships between producers, consumers and decomposers.

B5B9A4C0DFE601316C0468A86D17958E.description: Explain that most microorganisms do not cause disease and that many are beneficial to the environment.

B5B91AD0DFE601316C0368A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the factors that influence the number and kinds of organisms an ecosystem can support, including the resources that are available, the differences in temperature, the composition of the soil, any disease, the threat of predators, and competition from other organisms.

B5B85F90DFE601316C0168A86D17958E.description: Energy flows and matter recycles through an ecosystem.

B5B4CEA0DFE601316BF768A86D17958E.description: Explain that all living things reproduce in order to continue their species.

B5B47B50DFE601316BF668A86D17958E.description: Explain that the same genetic information is copied in each cell of a new organism.

B5B425E0DFE601316BF568A86D17958E.description: Explain that cells repeatedly divide to make more cells for growth and repair.

B5B334D0DFE601316BF368A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the human cells found in tissues and organs are similar to those of other animals, but somewhat different from cells found in plants.

B5B2E330DFE601316BF268A86D17958E.description: Explain that multicellular organisms have specialized cells, tissues, organs and organ systems that perform certain necessary functions, including digestion, respiration, reproduction, circulation, excretion, movement, control and coordination and protection from disease.

B5B28DC0DFE601316BF168A86D17958E.description: Recognize and describe the hierarchical organization of living systems, including cells, tissues, organs, organ systems, whole organisms, and ecosystems.

B5B23090DFE601316BF068A86D17958E.description: Recognize that cells use energy obtain from food, to conduct the functions necessary to sustain life, such as cell growth.

B5B1D980DFE601316BEF68A86D17958E.description: Explain that the way in which cells function is similar in all organisms.

B5B17390DFE601316BEE68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that all living things are composed of cells, and explain that while many organisms are single celled, such as yeast, others, including humans, are multicellular.

B5B0C810DFE601316BEC68A86D17958E.description: Categorize organisms into kingdoms that are currently recognized, according to shared characteristics.

B5B07050DFE601316BEB68A86D17958E.description: Identify ways in which living things can be grouped and organized, such as taxonomic groups of plants, animals and fungi.

B5AF9CC0DFE601316BE968A86D17958E.description: All living organisms have identifiable structures and characteristics that allow for survival (organisms, populations, and species).

B5AECED0DFE601316BE768A86D17958E.description: Understand that some form of science is used in most jobs/careers and that some jobs/careers specifically require knowledge of Earth science.

B5AE0D60DFE601316BE568A86D17958E.description: Provide examples of how to reduce waste through conservation, recycling, and reuse.

B5ADB740DFE601316BE468A86D17958E.description: Identify the most appropriate materials for a given design task with requirements for specific properties, such as weight, strength, hardness, and flexibility.

B5AD6730DFE601316BE368A86D17958E.description: Provide examples of products that man has developed which allow humans to do things that they could not do otherwise; and identify the natural materials used to produce these products.

B5ACC290DFE601316BE168A86D17958E.description: Read and interpret data from barometers, sling psychrometers and anemometers.

B5AC6710DFE601316BE068A86D17958E.description: Employ knowledge of basic weather symbols to read and interpret weather and topographic maps.

B5AC1250DFE601316BDF68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that satellites and Doppler radar can be used to observe or predict the weather.

B5AB6FE0DFE601316BDD68A86D17958E.description: Understand that technology is used to design tools that improve our ability to measure and observe the world.

B5AAB630DFE601316BDB68A86D17958E.description: The growth of scientific knowledge in Earth Space Science has been advanced through the development of technology and is used (alone or in combination with other sciences) to identify, understand and solve local and global issues.

B5AA5C80DFE601316BDA68A86D17958E.description: Describe the universe as being comprised of billions of galaxies, each containing many billions of stars; and explain that there are vast distances separating these galaxies and stars from one another and from the Earth.

B5A9A4B0DFE601316BD868A86D17958E.description: Describe objects such as asteroids, comets and meteors in terms of their characteristics and movement patterns.

B5A8F140DFE601316BD668A86D17958E.description: Explain that special units of measure, such as light years and astronomical units, are used to calculate distances in space.

B5A896F0DFE601316BD568A86D17958E.description: Define an astronomical unit as the distance from the Earth to the Sun.

B5A7CB70DFE601316BD368A86D17958E.description: The origin and evolution of galaxies and the universe demonstrate fundamental principles of physical science across vast distances and time.

B5A777A0DFE601316BD268A86D17958E.description: Describe man's perception of the constellations throughout history; and explain how he has used them to his advantage, including navigational purposes and to explain historical events.

B5A71C50DFE601316BD168A86D17958E.description: Explain the historical perspective of planetary exploration and man's achievements in space, beginning with Russia's Sputnik mission in 1957.

B5A67A80DFE601316BCF68A86D17958E.description: Explain how gravitational force affects objects in the Solar System (e.g., moons, tides, orbits, satellites).

B5A623B0DFE601316BCE68A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast planets based on data provided about size, composition, location, orbital movement, atmosphere, or surface features (includes moons).

B5A5CB20DFE601316BCD68A86D17958E.description: Explain why Earth and our Solar System appear to be somewhat unique, while acknowledging recent evidence that suggests similar systems exist in the universe.

B5A56150DFE601316BCC68A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects of gravitational force on the planets and their moons.

B5A50240DFE601316BCB68A86D17958E.description: Identify the characteristics and movement patterns of the planets in our Solar System and differentiate between them.

B5A43F20DFE601316BC968A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe seasonal, daylight and weather patterns as they relate to energy.

B5A3EC80DFE601316BC868A86D17958E.description: Recognize how the tilt of the Earth's axis and the Earth's revolution around the Sun affect seasons and weather patterns.

B5A33900DFE601316BC668A86D17958E.description: Recognize that of all the known planets, Earth appears to be somewhat unique; and describe the conditions that exist on Earth that allow it to support life.

B5A2CF10DFE601316BC568A86D17958E.description: Recognize and describe how the regular and predictable motions of the Earth and Moon explain certain Earth phenomena, such as day and night, the seasons, the year, shadows and the tides.

B5A20480DFE601316BC368A86D17958E.description: The Earth is part of a solar system, made up of distinct parts, which have temporal and spatial interrelationships.

B5A1A610DFE601316BC268A86D17958E.description: Explain that water quality has a direct effect on Earth's life forms.

B5A150C0DFE601316BC168A86D17958E.description: Explain the properties that make water an essential component of the Earth's system, including solvency and its ability to maintain a liquid state at most temperatures.

B5A09F10DFE601316BBF68A86D17958E.description: Describe the properties of soil, such as color, texture, capacity to retain water, and its ability to support plant life.

B5A02AA0DFE601316BBE68A86D17958E.description: Identify the components of soil and other factors, such as bacteria, fungi and worms, which influence its texture, fertility, and resistance to erosion.

B59FBAE0DFE601316BBD68A86D17958E.description: Explain how soil is formed from combinations of weathered rock and decomposed plant and animal remains, and that it contains living organisms.

B59F07F0DFE601316BBB68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that vibrations in materials set up wavelike disturbances that spread away from the source, as with earthquakes.

B59EB530DFE601316BBA68A86D17958E.description: Explain how some changes to the Earth's surface happen abruptly, as a result of landslides, earthquakes and volcanic eruptions; while other changes happen very slowly as a result of weathering, erosions and deposition of sediment caused by waves, wind, water and ice.

B59E5DE0DFE601316BB968A86D17958E.description: Recognize that things change in steady, repetitive, or irregular ways, or sometimes in more than one way at the same time.

B59DAC70DFE601316BB768A86D17958E.description: Explain that satellites can be used to view and track storms and Earth events, such as hurricanes and wild fires.

B59D5050DFE601316BB668A86D17958E.description: Recognize that images taken of the Earth from space can show its features and any changes in those features that appear over time.

B59CFA40DFE601316BB568A86D17958E.description: Observation Of The Earth From Space

B59CA700DFE601316BB468A86D17958E.description: Identify connections between fossil evidence and geological events, such as changes in atmospheric composition, movement of tectonic plates, and asteroid/comet impact; and develop a means of sequencing this evidence.

B59C3E00DFE601316BB368A86D17958E.description: Recognize that fossils offer important evidence relating to changes in life forms and environmental conditions over geologic time.

B59B96A0DFE601316BB168A86D17958E.description: Identify and distinguish between various landforms using a map and/or digital images.

B59B41D0DFE601316BB068A86D17958E.description: Describe and define the different landforms on the Earth's surface, such as coastlines, rivers, mountains, deltas, canyons, etc.

B59AEC60DFE601316BAF68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between renewable and nonrenewable resources.

B59A3860DFE601316BAD68A86D17958E.description: Describe how clouds affect weather and climate, including precipitation, reflecting light from the sun, and retaining heat energy emitted from the Earth's surface.

B599E510DFE601316BAC68A86D17958E.description: Describe weather in terms of temperature, wind speed and direction, precipitation, and cloud cover.

B5999180DFE601316BAB68A86D17958E.description: Explain the composition and structure of the Earth's atmosphere.

B5993980DFE601316BAA68A86D17958E.description: Identify weather patterns by tracking weather related events, such as hurricanes.

B598D3F0DFE601316BA968A86D17958E.description: Describe and make predictions about local and regional weather conditions using observation and data collection methods.

B5980590DFE601316BA768A86D17958E.description: The Earth and Earth materials, as we know them today, have developed over long periods of time, through constant change processes.

B5971AB0DFE601316BA568A86D17958E.description: Participate in simulation or role-playing activities in which students grapple with the ethics of complex issues.

B596B450DFE601316BA468A86D17958E.description: Collaborate with a network of learners by phone, video, virtual classroom platform.

B5961620DFE601316BA268A86D17958E.description: Participate in science competitions, where students are responsible for creating a product or participating in an event.

B595C2A0DFE601316BA168A86D17958E.description: Develop and execute a plan to collect and record accurate and complete data from various sources to solve a problem or answer a question; and gather and critically analyze data from a variety of sources.

B5950770DFE601316B9F68A86D17958E.description: Keep a journal of observations and investigations, and periodically evaluate entries to assess progress toward achieving the understanding of key ideas.

B5946400DFE601316B9D68A86D17958E.description: Articulate understanding of content through personal interaction and sharing with peers.

B59409B0DFE601316B9C68A86D17958E.description: Plan and develop team science projects.

B593B2C0DFE601316B9B68A86D17958E.description: Work in diverse pairs/teams to answer questions, solve problems and make decisions.

B592EA70DFE601316B9968A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of media tools to make oral and written presentations, which include written notes and descriptions, drawings, photos, and charts to communicate the procedures and results of an investigation.

B5923680DFE601316B9768A86D17958E.description: Use evidence collected from observations or other sources and use them to create models and explanations.

B591D310DFE601316B9668A86D17958E.description: Formulate a scientific question about phenomena, a problem, or an issue and using a broad range of tools and techniques; and plan and conduct an inquiry to address the question.

B590F2A0DFE601316B9468A86D17958E.description: Make sketches, graphs, and diagrams to explain ideas and to demonstrate the interconnections between systems.

B5909DD0DFE601316B9368A86D17958E.description: Apply new and unusual applications of existing knowledge to new and different situations.

B5904B70DFE601316B9268A86D17958E.description: Execute steps of scientific inquiry to engage in the problem-solving and decision making processes.

B58F9380DFE601316B9068A86D17958E.description: Use a wide range of tools and a variety of oral, written, and graphic formats to share information and results from observations and investigations.

B58EF330DFE601316B8E68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate tools to analyze and synthesize information (e.g., diagrams, flow charts, frequency tables, bar graphs, line graphs, stem-and-leaf plots) to draw conclusions and implications based on investigations of an issue or question.

B58EA0D0DFE601316B8D68A86D17958E.description: Collect real-time observations and data, synthesizing and building upon existing information (e.g., online databases, NOAA, EPA, USGS) to solve problems.

B58E4B80DFE601316B8C68A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of information access tools to locate, gather, and organize potential sources of scientific information to answer questions.

B58D9430DFE601316B8A68A86D17958E.description: Science Skills for Information, Communication and Media Literacy
comments: (from ICT Literacy Map for Science, www.21stcenturyskills.org)

B58D38A0DFE601316B8968A86D17958E.description: Evaluate technological designs using established criteria.

B58CD820DFE601316B8868A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the procedure for designing a product, including identifying a need, researching, brainstorming, selecting, developing a prototype, testing and evaluating.

B58C82A0DFE601316B8768A86D17958E.description: Identify problems/issues that can be addressed by design technology.

B58C24C0DFE601316B8668A86D17958E.description: Science and Technology, Technological Design and Application

B58BB0D0DFE601316B8568A86D17958E.description: Investigate environmental and resource management issues at scales that range from local to national to global.

B58B44A0DFE601316B8468A86D17958E.description: Explore how humans shape and control the environment while creating knowledge and developing new technologies.

B58AF130DFE601316B8368A86D17958E.description: Explore evidence that human-caused changes have consequences for the immediate environment as well as for other places and future times.

B58A9920DFE601316B8268A86D17958E.description: Design environmental investigations to answer particular questions.

B58A33F0DFE601316B8168A86D17958E.description: Develop, focus and explain questions about the environment and do environmental investigations.

B589E1A0DFE601316B8068A86D17958E.description: Common Environmental Issues, Natural Resources Management and Conservation

B5898330DFE601316B7F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate respect of one another's abilities and contributions to the group.

B5892E70DFE601316B7E68A86D17958E.description: Work collectively within a group toward a common goal.

B588D5B0DFE601316B7D68A86D17958E.description: Work effectively within a cooperative group setting, accepting and executing assigned roles and responsibilities.

B587B1B0DFE601316B7A68A86D17958E.description: Investigate the relationship between various landforms and wind currents.

B5875DD0DFE601316B7968A86D17958E.description: Diagram and label the structure of the primary components of representative organs in plants and animals.

B58708B0DFE601316B7868A86D17958E.description: Describe the structure and function of organs.

B58650F0DFE601316B7668A86D17958E.description: Discover how a system may stay the same because nothing is happening or because things are happening that exactly balance each other out.

B585D7F0DFE601316B7568A86D17958E.description: Understand that things change in steady, repetitive, or irregular ways, or sometimes in more than one way at the same time; often the best way to tell which kinds of change are happening is to make a table or graph of measurements.

B5851400DFE601316B7368A86D17958E.description: Analyze how finding out the biggest and smallest values of something are often as revealing as knowing what the usual value is.

B584C470DFE601316B7268A86D17958E.description: Understand that models are often used to think about processes that happen too slowly, too quickly, or on too small a scale to observe directly; or that are too vast to be changed deliberately; or that are potentially dangerous.

B5842210DFE601316B7068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how energy can be transformed from one form to another (e.g., from electrical energy to heat, light or mechanical energy).

B583CA20DFE601316B6F68A86D17958E.description: Compare a variety of forms of energy, including heat, light, sound, mechanical, electrical, and chemical energy.

B5835B50DFE601316B6E68A86D17958E.description: Estimate or predict the effect that making a change in one part of the system will have on other parts, and on the system as a whole.

B582FAE0DFE601316B6D68A86D17958E.description: Discover that collections of pieces (e.g., powders, marbles, sugar cubes or wooden blocks) may have properties that the individual pieces do not.

B5829EA0DFE601316B6C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that thinking about things as systems means looking for how every part relates to others.

B581D7E0DFE601316B6A68A86D17958E.description: Realize that if more than one variable changes at the same time in an experiment, the outcome of the experiment may not be clearly attributable to any one of the variables.

B58175D0DFE601316B6968A86D17958E.description: Explain that sometimes similar investigations get different results because of unexpected differences in the things being investigated, the methods used, or the circumstances in which the investigation is carried out, and sometimes just because of uncertainties of observations.

B58124D0DFE601316B6868A86D17958E.description: Describe how results of similar and repeated investigations may vary and suggest possible explanations for variations.

B580D2E0DFE601316B6768A86D17958E.description: Explain that scientists do not pay much attention to claims about how something works unless they are backed up with evidence that can be confirmed with a logical argument.

B57F8A00DFE601316B6468A86D17958E.description: Explain how a hypothesis is a direct extension of a scientific idea and therefore makes that idea "testable."

B57F39D0DFE601316B6368A86D17958E.description: Determine if the results of an experiment support or fail to support the scientific idea tested.

B57E9490DFE601316B6168A86D17958E.description: Draw appropriate conclusions based on data collected.

B57E3F90DFE601316B6068A86D17958E.description: Identify patterns and relationships in data and formulate basic explanations.

B57DE600DFE601316B5F68A86D17958E.description: Compare and display data in a variety of student or computer generated formats (such as diagrams, flow charts, tables, bar graphs, line graphs, scatter plots, and histograms).

B57D90D0DFE601316B5E68A86D17958E.description: Make and record observations using a predetermined format.

B57D40A0DFE601316B5D68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate tools to organize, represent, analyze and explain data.

B57CEF90DFE601316B5C68A86D17958E.description: Representing and Understanding Results of Investigations

B57C9C90DFE601316B5B68A86D17958E.description: Follow the teacher's instructions in performing experiments, following all appropriate safety rules and procedures.

B57C45E0DFE601316B5A68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate tools to collect and record data.

B57BDC70DFE601316B5968A86D17958E.description: Carry out simple student or teacher-developed procedures or experiments.

B57B1FB0DFE601316B5768A86D17958E.description: Incorporate components of good experimental design, such as controls and multiple trials, into investigations.

B57AC2C0DFE601316B5668A86D17958E.description: Identify and utilize appropriate tools/technology for collecting data in designing investigations.

B57A4690DFE601316B5568A86D17958E.description: Design and record a simple step-by-step procedure to follow in order to carry out a fair test of a scientific question.

B5799E60DFE601316B5368A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between those questions that can be answered by science and those that cannot.

B5794E40DFE601316B5268A86D17958E.description: Determine which observations will be helpful to a given investigation.

B578FE90DFE601316B5168A86D17958E.description: Ask questions about relationships between and among observations.

B578A8A0DFE601316B5068A86D17958E.description: Compare methods of classification for a specific purpose.

B5780440DFE601316B4E68A86D17958E.description: Use a classification key, such as a dichotomous key, to identify and distinguish among members of a group or set.

B577B120DFE601316B4D68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate units and precision of metric measurement when recording data.

B5775AB0DFE601316B4C68A86D17958E.description: Identify and investigate similarities and differences among observations and sets of observations.

B576F790DFE601316B4B68A86D17958E.description: Plan observations based on a given purpose.

B57693C0DFE601316B4A68A86D17958E.description: Make observations and record measurements using a variety of tools and instruments.
