2EA9A4641D044B0D8123A0300C600FDD.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

38B81561D70749E9BB50F53D5786871C.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

3475260BD1DD487FA8843DC031F2544C.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

33C699CE61964D62ACC3EF309A5CD019.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

F5A9BA8CDF5A4F34B235CAC80A1A0713.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

62B8BEFC5BFF4D61A2586A14596577B9.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

81EDEC2B951C42BBB6422F0A3704D1C9.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

00AAF168F775492DA21A049B8C7301D8.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

5138B8E0133C439699B964CFCBCAE891.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

80961E40E3104A4E88F103C7508D9C64.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

69C8092C5C51479E94E6E98027029571.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

A4AB37B948704199A7825641FEED7BC5.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

E57B4436E8D8495CBBFD33C12566D862.description: Read on-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

8CF9A619C9B7402CA8B4EE0F2C5014D7.description: Read on-level text with purpose and understanding.

8F47083EB030468B84A8D58FE74591D9.description: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension.

B9F035908FE24715A987A8C5B8CC9FBE.description: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words.

2CD2A86825CE40D68E42F4EBE5AD2616.description: Distinguish long from short vowel sounds in spoken single-syllable words.

95506F175E254DA4B2D659DBA6C88ECD.description: Recognize the distinguishing features of a sentence (e.g., first word, capitalization, ending punctuation).

4E97F41E61B3428B925E2549C68A7BA7.description: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print.

3FC1909B31234420A8014821C3A78E7D.description: With prompting and support, read informational texts appropriately complex for grade 1.

9FB022A9D5A74D8397321FD215CEED03.description: Identify the reasons an author gives to support points in a text.

67938EEA762A41119EA93335CD20446A.description: Use the illustrations and details in a text to describe its key ideas.

8DBEC42593954623AFA5FFF7069FF3C5.description: Know and use various text features (e.g., headings, tables of contents, glossaries, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text.

6DBFADC018B748C695300CD1CFC9FDBA.description: Identify the main topic and retell key details of a text.

F68A9BEA75BF4F03B5555158F780DAE0.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.

0D59AE91A27A48DA9DF2F023039A50DA.description: With prompting and support, read prose and poetry of appropriate complexity for grade 1.

8430E9E97B424EC0BBD02269B04B5CC3.description: Compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in stories.

3C9DAA7D6E714508A45DF3F0F2DC396A.description: Use illustrations and details in a story to describe its characters, setting, or events.

49B2417A6DA8408EA95E28ACECE05CC7.description: Identify who is telling the story at various points in a text.

A7CE147521BC4CE58D0C4F5C39EB245A.description: Explain major differences between books that tell stories and books that give information, drawing on a wide reading of a range of text types.

75B7EF57AC0242068500D15B8CC090BC.description: Identify words and phrases in stories or poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.

A052AE532D6343B5B7A37E04C87A681B.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

441BAAEA8064421195202C70C16877D1.description: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (e.g., bullheaded, willful, firm, persistent, resolute).

2C8589A57DEC43B280472EAB08039FDA.description: Use the relationship between particular words to better understand each of the words.

A4B3613ADAF44CCCA355FF0072996AB4.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g. verbal irony, puns) in context.

B3F78164AF7341498A7A05D3A9FFBE55.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

F254748B48DD4C87B5A257A64BC4F72C.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

5C56F4B8E83B47B48BD1E83C1305AB7D.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

043A45BA2D734455B6DA1B2B84153353.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words or phrases based on grade 8 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

5B3FD1F6E39C420BACD2AB65014B3318.description: Use verbs in the active and passive voice and in the conditional and subjunctive mood to achieve particular effects (e.g., emphasizing the actor or the action; expressing uncertainty or describing a state contrary to fact).

D175A65CB9E24F02A3EA44DD8364F4A9.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

E9E733867D074AF3A09E3B9A4F765097.description: Use an ellipsis to indicate an omission.

3573F1CB9833448BAAA054ABA73FFD72.description: Use punctuation (comma, ellipsis, dash) to indicate a pause or break.

EB454B0BB6494B519E29371F1154CCED.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

F6BD05A277F840D697ED65B244B92F4F.description: Form and use verbs in the active and passive voice.

33506F77814848E282406B60661B3CBA.description: Explain the function of verbals (gerunds, participles, infinitives) in general and their function in particular sentences.

840DABC8F74F4B78835319D181F62A2D.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

BC4134C30E964153B7974FD9395C201D.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

DF28FEDFDB474A29AE8DB231E25748F2.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

E8A8C3A955864D7EAE9DEA31936303A4.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

815D4CC5D84048648200FA1DA4608CD2.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.

document.title: NH Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

AF99E042AEF54865821AE93D8192B92B.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.

ECC88FB6904B43C0BB53CEE633BA4CC3.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.

A06F02B048A148B2B90A565A89D2DCD1.description: Use functions to model relationships between quantities.

F1A811587FEF4B2DAD5DCCDBE034252C.description: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear.
comments: For example, the function A = s² giving the area of a square as a function of its side length is not linear because its graph contains the points (1,1), (2,4) and (3,9), which are not on a straight line.

9E976BDFE76C4A449991387A3DF20145.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).
comments: For example, given a linear function represented by a table of values and a linear function represented by an algebraic expression, determine which function has the greater rate of change.

00C8E85502A640C7867F1D4E568F087E.description: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output.
comments: Function notation is not required in Grade 8.

D3245E738D824CA18F3BD70A441B4857.description: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables.
comments: For example, collect data from students in your class on whether or not they have a curfew on school nights and whether or not they have assigned chores at home. Is there evidence that those who have a curfew also tend to have chores?

01692A72C20148B6A1070447FA6BF0F9.description: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept.
comments: For example, in a linear model for a biology experiment, interpret a slope of 1.5 cm/hr as meaning that an additional hour of sunlight each day is associated with an additional 1.5 cm in mature plant height.

B9206FB051DD460E99AE0D1C771CEF85.description: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.

7D3899B8E55447049AA4F6F6FE392D96.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.

3A25367212974ADB97682C834E8605C6.description: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data.

B2D0451E79AB4B9583C975ED927346C5.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables.
comments: For example, given coordinates for two pairs of points, determine whether the line through the first pair of points intersects the line through the second pair.

84D91D0E30314B0F8B5B7B09B0F613D5.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection.
comments: For example, 3x + 2y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 6 have no solution because 3x + 2y cannot simultaneously be 5 and 6.

EEF7621755054DED8DCAA08A48A53442.description: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.

26F5A699B6F94BC49A1D3408DDE2DD09.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

2A779EBD62BE44EB898962807DEBA192.description: Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and collecting like terms.

954270D6D5FB4010859CFC7C709704CF.description: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b results (where a and b are different numbers).

56E9BFA627E244CDB11B036C16B795CB.description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

0BC2F6DAB9E54C5A9D8B718340750CEF.description: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

98681DEABC6D4A32BFBDD4795B401308.description: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.

comments: For example, compare a distance-time graph to a distance-time equation to determine which of two moving objects has greater speed.
EA18E1A3BADF4C948604F28240B66F0B.description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways.

51F74FB253324A72913DB834C1619216.description: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations.

20EE4BD0579A415CA44719F217BA92A1.description: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.

13C7A0760E864EA390EBB8C50A2B2D92.description: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one is than the other.
comments: For example, estimate the population of the United States as 3 × 10<sup>8</sup> and the population of the world as 7 × 10<sup>9</sup>, and determine that the world population is more than 20 times larger.

032993EB8D8C4F4C8591C7F1E687BB5F.description: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Know that √2 is irrational.

4BC53B7FD0FF41ABAF4DE3AA7927388F.description: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.
comments: For example, 3² × 3<sup>-5</sup> = 3<sup>-3</sup> = 1/3³ = 1/27.

0595209172864F07A90D81E5F2BB75A4.description: Work with radicals and integer exponents.

BD7D607DA74A4BE5893DBB46236DF4C1.description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions (e.g., π²).
comments: For example, by truncating the decimal expansion of √2, show that √2 is between 1 and 2, then between 1.4 and 1.5, and explain how to continue on to get better approximations.

414E24B1F516429C920B684CF98BD166.description: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually, and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually into a rational number.

A5D5ED6FD0D4436DA630AB8E35D86CDC.description: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers.

4D9C2882A2A5440B85DA203668E9341C.description: Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

390036F7152B4317ACD6BB1E63B8C2D4.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.

B7E88C0ACE414D88AA2D2349D69277EE.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.

comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.
793710E581694D21ADD682F2F3120C0D.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

F7DB602CE8C24DF3AB04E2871BF88F8B.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

0C237E15799F439587FF6A2D1FC91C30.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.
4D23E7103F3442FFAA3444F9A50F9741.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

B916C360DFE60131725768A86D17958E.description: demonstrate the ability to read a full instrumental or vocal score by describing how the elements of music are used and explaining all transpositions and clefs;

B91676E0DFE60131725668A86D17958E.description: (for choral/instrumental ensemble/class) sight-read, accurately and expressively, music with a difficulty level of 3 on a scale of 1 to 6.

B9162990DFE60131725568A86D17958E.description: demonstrate the ability to read an instrumental or vocal score of up to four staves by describing how the elements of music are used;

B9158230DFE60131725368A86D17958E.description: compose music, demonstrating imagination and technical skill in applying the principles of composition.

B9151FB0DFE60131725268A86D17958E.description: compose and arrange music for voices and various acoustic and electronic instruments, demonstrating knowledge of the ranges and traditional usage of the sound sources.

B914C540DFE60131725168A86D17958E.description: arrange pieces for voices or instruments other than those for which the pieces were written in ways that preserve or enhance the expressive effect of the music;

B9146A00DFE60131725068A86D17958E.description: compose music in several distinct styles, demonstrating creativity in using the elements of music for expressive effect;

B91415D0DFE60131724F68A86D17958E.description: Compose and arrange music within specified guidelines.

B913BE20DFE60131724E68A86D17958E.description: improvise original melodies in a variety of styles, over given chord progressions, each in a consistent style, meter, and tonality.

B9137110DFE60131724D68A86D17958E.description: improvise stylistically appropriate harmonization/homophonic parts in a variety of styles;

B9132310DFE60131724C68A86D17958E.description: improvise original melodies over given chord progressions, each in a consistent style, meter, and tonality.

B912CFF0DFE60131724B68A86D17958E.description: improvise rhythmic and melodic variations on given pentatonic melodies and melodies in major and minor keys;

B911B5E0DFE60131724868A86D17958E.description: perform with expression and technical accuracy a large and varied repertoire of instrumental literature with a difficulty level of 5, on a scale of 1 to 6.

B9116A80DFE60131724768A86D17958E.description: perform in small ensembles with one student on a part.

B9111FA0DFE60131724668A86D17958E.description: perform an appropriate part in an ensemble, demonstrating well-developed ensemble skills.

B910D1C0DFE60131724568A86D17958E.description: perform with expression and technical accuracy a large and varied repertoire of instrumental literature with a difficulty level of 4, on a scale of 1 to 6;

B9108430DFE60131724468A86D17958E.description: Perform on instruments, alone and with others, a varied repertoire of music.

B9102810DFE60131724368A86D17958E.description: sing in small ensembles with one student on each part.

B90FCE90DFE60131724268A86D17958E.description: sing music written in more than four parts;

B90F75C0DFE60131724168A86D17958E.description: sing with expression and technical accuracy a large and varied repertoire of vocal literature with a difficulty level of 5 on a scale of 1 to 6;

B90F2480DFE60131724068A86D17958E.description: sing music written in four parts, with and without accompaniment, demonstrating well-developed ensemble skills.

B90ED610DFE60131723F68A86D17958E.description: sing with expression and technical accuracy a large and varied repertoire of vocal literature in more than one language with a difficulty level of 4 on a scale of 1 to 6, including some songs performed from memory;

B90E8430DFE60131723E68A86D17958E.description: Sing, alone and with others, a varied repertoire of music.

B90BCCB0DFE60131723668A86D17958E.description: compose a list of questions to identify specific skills and knowledge needed to enter a particular dance-related career and seek answers from a variety of community sources.

B90B7C70DFE60131723568A86D17958E.description: discuss how skills developed in dance are applicable to a variety of life skills.

B90B2500DFE60131723468A86D17958E.description: identify and discuss a variety of employment and financial opportunities for people who choose a career in dance;

B90AC960DFE60131723368A86D17958E.description: create an extensive list of dance-related careers;

B90A7A40DFE60131723268A86D17958E.description: describe ways in which dance influences everyday life;

B90A2A50DFE60131723168A86D17958E.description: Identify the range of careers in the field of dance.

B909E040DFE60131723068A86D17958E.description: create a project using media technologies, such as video and computers, that present dance in a new or enhanced form.

B9099270DFE60131722F68A86D17958E.description: compare choreographic works to other artwork from the same culture and time period;

B9093C10DFE60131722E68A86D17958E.description: create an interdisciplinary project based on a theme identified by the student.

B908DD90DFE60131722D68A86D17958E.description: explore/discuss how other forms of communication, such as, visual art, spoken word, music or video can enhance or alter the ideas conveyed in a dance, drawing on examples from their own dances and those of others;

B90884E0DFE60131722C68A86D17958E.description: create a project the reveals similarities between dance and other disciplines;

B9082940DFE60131722B68A86D17958E.description: Make connections between dance and other disciplines.

B907BC50DFE60131722A68A86D17958E.description: analyze challenges facing professional performers in maintaining healthy lifestyles.

B9075D00DFE60131722968A86D17958E.description: analyze and discuss historical and cultural images of the body and compare these images to presentation of the body in contemporary media.

B906DD10DFE60131722868A86D17958E.description: communicate how lifestyle choices, such as smoking, drug use or diet, affect the dancer;

B9068B50DFE60131722768A86D17958E.description: reflect upon their own progress and personal growth during their study of dance; examine how fluency in dance can support success and confidence in other areas;

B9063830DFE60131722668A86D17958E.description: Make connections between dance and healthful living.

B905EAE0DFE60131722568A86D17958E.description: compare the role and significance of dance and dancers in North America with other cultures, considering the historical period and social/political contexts.

B9059870DFE60131722468A86D17958E.description: perform or discuss the traditions and techniques of folk forms, such as Morris dance, Irish step dance or American Hopi Indian dance, placing each in an historical or cultural context.

B9053C70DFE60131722368A86D17958E.description: perform and describe similarities and differences among a broad spectrum of folk, social, and/or theatrical dances or dance forms from the 20th century;

B904EB20DFE60131722268A86D17958E.description: perform or discuss the traditions and techniques of a classical dance form;

B9049A90DFE60131722168A86D17958E.description: Recognize and demonstrate dance in various cultures and historical periods.

B9044850DFE60131722068A86D17958E.description: analyze the style of a choreographer or cultural dance form; identify characteristics of the style or dance form which make it distinctive from other styles and dance forms; then create a movement study in that style.

B903EC90DFE60131721F68A86D17958E.description: analyze issues of ethnicity, gender, social/economic class, age, and/or physical condition in relation dance

B90398E0DFE60131721E68A86D17958E.description: establish a set of aesthetic criteria and apply it in evaluating their own choreography and that of others;

B9033F10DFE60131721D68A86D17958E.description: create a dance and revise it over time, articulating the reasons for their artistic decisions, considering what was lost and gained by those decisions;

B902E4F0DFE60131721C68A86D17958E.description: Apply and demonstrate critical and creative thinking skills in dance.

B9028B60DFE60131721B68A86D17958E.description: create and/or critique a dance that explores a contemporary social theme, analyzing how the work accomplishes or does not accomplish its intentions.

B9023A70DFE60131721A68A86D17958E.description: compare and contrast how meaning is communicated in two of their own choreographic works;

B901E3C0DFE60131721968A86D17958E.description: analyze and discuss a performer's ability to communicate meaning to an audience.

B9018570DFE60131721868A86D17958E.description: examine ways that a dance conveys various meanings from a variety of perspectives;

B90123F0DFE60131721768A86D17958E.description: discuss and evaluate how movement choices communicate ideas in dance;

B900D5A0DFE60131721668A86D17958E.description: Recognize dance as a way to create and communicate meaning.

B9008470DFE60131721568A86D17958E.description: create a movement study focusing on dance phrases that use complex rhythmic and musical elements.

B9002470DFE60131721468A86D17958E.description: demonstrate further development and refinement of the proficient achievement standards to create a small group dance with coherence and aesthetic unity;

B8FFD0B0DFE60131721368A86D17958E.description: describe how a choreographer developed and organized the basic movement content in a particular dance.

B8FF7960DFE60131721268A86D17958E.description: create a movement study for two or more dancers;

B8FF2430DFE60131721168A86D17958E.description: create a movement study focusing on dynamic change and transitions;

B8FEC520DFE60131721068A86D17958E.description: explore choreographic structure by creating a movement phrase that can be rearranged according to various compositional forms;

B8FE6840DFE60131720F68A86D17958E.description: use improvisation to generate movement for choreography;

B8FDA7C0DFE60131720D68A86D17958E.description: demonstrate a high level of consistency and reliability in performing technical skills.

B8FD5130DFE60131720C68A86D17958E.description: improve dance technique through self-evaluation and correction;

B8FCFF90DFE60131720B68A86D17958E.description: improve performance of movement and technical skills by using a broad dynamic range.

B8FC5090DFE60131720968A86D17958E.description: identify and demonstrate longer and more complex movement;

B8FBF3F0DFE60131720868A86D17958E.description: refine appropriate body alignment, body-part articulation, strength, flexibility, agility, and coordination in locomotor and axial movements;

B8FB9EB0DFE60131720768A86D17958E.description: Identify and demonstrate movement elements and skills in performing dance.

document.title: K-12 Science Literacy New Hampshire Curriculum Framework

B6FA3650DFE601316EAB68A86D17958E.description: Explain the kinds of applications of knowledge and skills necessary for jobs/careers specific to the physical sciences.

B6F98EB0DFE601316EA968A86D17958E.description: Explain the benefits of standardization of parts.

B6F939E0DFE601316EA868A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship between energy and power.

B6F8D8C0DFE601316EA768A86D17958E.description: Calculate the efficiency of an engine, and explain why a perfectly efficient engine is impossible.

B6F761E0DFE601316EA668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and explain how an engine converts chemical energy in the form of fuel, into mechanical energy in the form of motion.

B6F70550DFE601316EA568A86D17958E.description: Explain that power systems have a source of energy, a process, loads, and some have a feedback system.

B6F69A90DFE601316EA468A86D17958E.description: Social Issues (Local and Global) Energy, Power, and Transportation Manufacturing

B6F60C70DFE601316EA368A86D17958E.description: Identify tools, such as thermostats and thermal sensors, and explain their use in environmental control systems.

B6F51D80DFE601316EA168A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the basic principles of energy, work and power are related to design technology.

B6F41320DFE601316E9F68A86D17958E.description: The growth of scientific knowledge in Physical Science has been advanced through the development of technology and is used (alone or in combination with other sciences) to identify, understand and solve local and global issues.

B6F3B070DFE601316E9E68A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects on wavelength and frequency as electromagnetic waves interact with matter (e.g., light diffraction, blue sky).

B6F35C90DFE601316E9D68A86D17958E.description: Apply the concepts of inertia, motion, and momentum to predict and explain situations involving forces and motion, including stationary objects and collisions.

B6F30790DFE601316E9C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that apparent changes in wavelength can provide information about changes in motion; explain that the observed wavelength of a wave depends upon the relative motion of the source and the observer; and relate these to the differences between shorter and longer wavelengths.

B6F2A8F0DFE601316E9B68A86D17958E.description: Interpret and apply the laws of motion to determine the effects of forces on the motion of objects.

B6F1F810DFE601316E9968A86D17958E.description: Given information (e.g., graphs, data, diagrams), use the relationships between or among force, mass, velocity, momentum, and acceleration to predict and explain the motion of objects.

B6F1A260DFE601316E9868A86D17958E.description: Describe the difference between materials that contain equal proportions of positive and negative charges and those that have a very small excess or deficit of negative charges.

B6F14A50DFE601316E9768A86D17958E.description: Recognize that different kinds of materials respond to electric forces in various ways; and differentiate between insulators, semiconductors, conductors and superconductors.

B6F0ED90DFE601316E9668A86D17958E.description: Recognize that electromagnetic forces exist within and between atoms.

B6F08380DFE601316E9568A86D17958E.description: Compare the strength of nuclear, electromagnetic and gravitational forces; and explain that the strength of nuclear forces account for the great amounts of energy released from the nuclear reactions in atomic or hydrogen bombs, and in the Sun and other stars.

B6F01BB0DFE601316E9468A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the strength of the gravitational force between two masses is proportional to the masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

B6EFA870DFE601316E9368A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the strength of the electric force between two charged objects is proportional to the charges and, as with gravitation, is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

B6EF1860DFE601316E9268A86D17958E.description: Explain that magnetic forces are related to the action of electrons and can be thought of as different aspects of a single electromagnetic force; and describe how the interplay of these forces is the basis for electric motors, generators, radio, television, and many other modern technologies.

B6EE6390DFE601316E9068A86D17958E.description: The motion of an object is affected by force.

B6EE0E30DFE601316E8F68A86D17958E.description: Using information provided about chemical changes, draw conclusions about the energy flow in a given chemical reaction (e.g., exothermic reactions, endothermic reactions).

B6EDB360DFE601316E8E68A86D17958E.description: Describe how electrons flow easily in some materials, such as metals, whereas in insulating materials, such as glass, they can hardly flow at all.

B6ED5740DFE601316E8D68A86D17958E.description: Explain that nuclear reactions convert a fraction of the mass of interacting particles into energy and release much greater amounts of energy than atomic interactions.

B6ECF4D0DFE601316E8C68A86D17958E.description: Explain that waves, such as light, seismic, sound waves, have energy and can transfer energy when they interact with matter.

B6ECA130DFE601316E8B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationship between heat and temperature, explaining that heat energy consists of the random motion and vibrations of atoms, molecules, and ions; and that the higher the temperature, the greater the atomic or molecular motion.

B6EC4BB0DFE601316E8A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the human eye can only see a narrow range of wavelengths within the electromagnetic spectrum; and explain how the variations of wavelength within that range of visible light are perceived as differences in color.

B6EBF380DFE601316E8968A86D17958E.description: Explain the range of the electromagnetic spectrum as it relates to both wavelength and energy; and provide examples of practical applications of the different wavelengths in the spectrum.

B6EB8E90DFE601316E8868A86D17958E.description: Describe how the energy associated with individual atoms and molecules can be used to identify the substances they comprise; and explain that each kind of atom or molecule can gain or lose energy only in particular discrete amounts, absorbing and emitting light only at wavelengths corresponding to these amounts.

B6EB26C0DFE601316E8768A86D17958E.description: Provide examples of how kinetic and potential energy can be transformed from one to the other.

B6EAC530DFE601316E8668A86D17958E.description: Explain that all energy can be considered to be either kinetic energy, potential energy, or energy contained by a field.

B6EA1650DFE601316E8468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how transformations of energy produce some energy in the form of heat and therefore the efficiency of the system is reduced (chemical, biological, and physical systems).

B6E99DE0DFE601316E8368A86D17958E.description: Identify the variety of structures that may be formed from the bonding of carbon atoms, and describe their roles in various chemical reactions, including those required for life processes.

B6E92370DFE601316E8268A86D17958E.description: Recognize that a large number of important reactions involve the transfer of either electrons or hydrogen ions between reacting ions, molecules, or atoms.

B6E8C7E0DFE601316E8168A86D17958E.description: Explain that chemical reactions can be accelerated by catalysts, such as enzymes.

B6E86BD0DFE601316E8068A86D17958E.description: Explain that chemical reactions either release or consume energy.

B6E7B9B0DFE601316E7E68A86D17958E.description: Explain relationships between and among electric charges, magnetic fields, electromagnetic forces, and atomic particles.

B6E751E0DFE601316E7D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the rates of chemical reactions can vary greatly; and identify the factors that influence these reaction rates, such as how often the reacting atoms and molecules encounter one another, the temperature, and the properties of the reacting species, including shape.

B6E6FC20DFE601316E7C68A86D17958E.description: Explain that compounds are formed through both ionic and covalent bonding.

B6E6A5C0DFE601316E7B68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that atoms interact with one another by transferring or sharing electrons that are furthest from the nucleus; and explain that the outer electrons govern the chemical properties of an element.

B6E64120DFE601316E7A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain that atoms may be bonded together into molecules or formula units (crystalline solids).

B6E56AB0DFE601316E7868A86D17958E.description: Energy is necessary for change to occur in matter. Energy can be stored, transferred and transformed, but cannot be destroyed.

B6E51890DFE601316E7768A86D17958E.description: Explain how properties of elements and the location of elements on the periodic table are related.

B6E4C4B0DFE601316E7668A86D17958E.description: Use physical and chemical properties as determined through an investigation to identify a substance.

B6E46B60DFE601316E7568A86D17958E.description: Explain that states of matter rely on the arrangement and motion of molecules; and differentiate between the structures of solids, liquids, and gases.

B6E40630DFE601316E7468A86D17958E.description: Explain that radioactive materials are unstable and undergo spontaneous nuclear reactions, which emit particles and/or wavelike radiation.

B6E39090DFE601316E7368A86D17958E.description: Explain how the chemical properties of an element are governed by the electron configuration of atoms, and describe how atoms interact with one another by transferring or sharing the outermost electrons.

B6E33BB0DFE601316E7268A86D17958E.description: Determine whether an atom is either electrically neutral or an ion by referring to its number of electrons.

B6E2E610DFE601316E7168A86D17958E.description: Explain that the physical properties of a compound are determined by its molecular structure and the interactions among the molecules.

B6E233E0DFE601316E6F68A86D17958E.description: Model and explain the structure of an atom or explain how an atom's electron configuration, particularly the outermost electron(s), determines how that atom can interact with other atoms.

B6E1D140DFE601316E6E68A86D17958E.description: Scientific thought about atoms has changed over time. Using information (narratives or models of atoms) provided, cite evidence that changed our understanding of the atom and the development of atomic theory.

B6E173E0DFE601316E6D68A86D17958E.description: Define isotopes; recognize that most elements have two or more isotopes; and explain that although the number of neutrons has little affect on how the atom interacts with others, they do affect the mass and stability of the nucleus.

B6E10E70DFE601316E6C68A86D17958E.description: Explain that neutrons and protons are made up of even smaller constituents.

B6E0ABB0DFE601316E6B68A86D17958E.description: Recognize how elements are arranged in the periodic table; and explain how this arrangement illustrates the repeating patterns among elements with similar properties, such as the relationship between atomic number and atomic mass.

B6E044D0DFE601316E6A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and describe the structure of an atom and explain how the major components interact with one another.

B6DF8F80DFE601316E6868A86D17958E.description: All living and nonliving things are composed of matter having characteristic properties that distinguish one substance from another (independent of size/amount of substance).

B6DEE400DFE601316E6668A86D17958E.description: Explain the kinds of applications of knowledge and skills necessary for jobs/careers specific to the life sciences.

B6DE0930DFE601316E6468A86D17958E.description: Explain how advances in agriculture made using biotechnology have directly affected the food production over the past 100 years; and that this change has profoundly affected societies all over the globe, making larger populations and urban centers a possibility.

B6DDAFF0DFE601316E6368A86D17958E.description: Recognize that biotechnology is used in many areas, such as agriculture, pharmaceuticals, the environment, and genetic engineering; and understand that it requires extensive knowledge of the systems being changed.

B6DD58B0DFE601316E6268A86D17958E.description: Describe aspects of the medical system available to help people in New Hampshire, including: prevention programs, vaccines and pharmaceuticals, hospitals and rehabilitation facilities.

B6DD0120DFE601316E6168A86D17958E.description: Describe ways technology can support and improve our understanding of environmental issues.

B6DCA460DFE601316E6068A86D17958E.description: Social Issues (Local And Global) Medical Technology and Biotechnology

B6DC3A10DFE601316E5F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the use and benefits of equipment such as light microscopes, transmission electron microscopes, scanning electron microscopes, spectrophotometers, probes, and robotics to the study of the life sciences.

B6DB7660DFE601316E5D68A86D17958E.description: Understand that technology is designed with a particular function in mind, and principles of life science are useful in creating technology for the life sciences.

B6DB21B0DFE601316E5C68A86D17958E.description: Describe ways in which technology has increased our understanding of the life sciences.

B6DA68A0DFE601316E5A68A86D17958E.description: The growth of scientific knowledge in Life Science has been advanced through the development of technology and is used (alone or in combination with other sciences) to identify, understand and solve local and global issues.

B6DA10F0DFE601316E5968A86D17958E.description: Explain how the immune system, endocrine system, or nervous system works and draw conclusions about how systems interact to maintain homeostasis in the human body.

B6D9B480DFE601316E5868A86D17958E.description: Explain how the immune system functions to prevent and fight disease.

B6D94C30DFE601316E5768A86D17958E.description: Describe how the length and quality of human life are influenced by many factors, including sanitation, diet, medical care, gender, genes, and environmental conditions and personal health behaviors.

B6D86D40DFE601316E5568A86D17958E.description: Use evidence to make and support conclusions about the ways that humans or other organisms are affected by environmental factors or heredity (e.g., pathogens, diseases, medical advances, pollution, mutations).

B6D81890DFE601316E5468A86D17958E.description: Explain that gene mutation in a cell can result in uncontrolled division, which is called cancer; and describe how exposure of cells to certain chemicals and radiation increase mutation, and thus the chance for cancer.

B6D7C360DFE601316E5368A86D17958E.description: Describe how some drugs mimic or block the molecules involved in transmitting nerve or hormone signals and explain how this disturbs the normal operations of the brain and body.

B6D76960DFE601316E5268A86D17958E.description: Describe and provide examples of how new medical techniques, efficient health care delivery systems, improved sanitation, and a more complete understanding of the nature of disease provides today's humans a better chance of staying healthier than their forebears.

B6D70CE0DFE601316E5168A86D17958E.description: Explain that vaccines were developed to reduce or eliminate diseases; and provide examples of how these medical advances have proven to be successful.

B6D6AD00DFE601316E5068A86D17958E.description: Explain that disease in organisms can be caused by intrinsic failures of the system or infection by other organisms, and describe as well as provide examples of how some diseases are caused by: the breakdown in cellular function, congenital conditions, genetic disorders, malnutrition, and emotional health, including stress.

B6D604A0DFE601316E4E68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the functions of all the human body systems are interrelated at a chemical level and how they maintain homeostasis.

B6D5AF40DFE601316E4D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the immune system, endocrine system, and nervous system can affect the homeostasis of an organism.

B6D4F3C0DFE601316E4B68A86D17958E.description: Humans are similar to other species in many ways, and yet are unique among Earth's life forms.

B6CFB4D0DFE601316E3D68A86D17958E.description: Given a scenario, provide evidence that demonstrates how sexual reproduction results in a great variety of possible gene combinations and contributes to natural selection (e.g., Darwin's finches, isolation of a species, Tay Sach's disease).

B6CF4500DFE601316E3C68A86D17958E.description: Use pedigree charts and Punnet Squares to determine patterns of inheritance.

B6CEE560DFE601316E3B68A86D17958E.description: Explain the concepts of Mendelian genetics.

B6CE7F40DFE601316E3A68A86D17958E.description: Explain that gene mutations and new combinations may have a variety of effects on the organism, including positive and negative ones, or none at all.

B6CE2700DFE601316E3968A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe ways genes may be changed and combined to create genetic variation within a species.

B6CDCBA0DFE601316E3868A86D17958E.description: Analyze present day data and research in areas, including antibiotic resistance in bacteria, changes in viral genomes, such as bird flu, and DNA sequencing; and relate it to the concepts of natural selection.

B6CD5D60DFE601316E3768A86D17958E.description: Recognize how a species' chance of survival increases with each variation of an organism within the species; and explain how, in the event of a major global change, the greater the diversity of species on Earth, the greater the chance for survival of life.

B6CCD2E0DFE601316E3668A86D17958E.description: Explain the diversity and unity of past and present life forms on Earth using currently accepted theories.

B6CC7CD0DFE601316E3568A86D17958E.description: Explain the concept of natural selection.

B6CBB970DFE601316E3368A86D17958E.description: Given information about living or extinct organisms, cite evidence to explain the frequency of inherited characteristics of organisms in a population; or explain the evolution of varied structures (with defined functions) that affected the organisms' survival in a specific environment (e.g., giraffe, wind pollination of flowers).

B6CB5DB0DFE601316E3268A86D17958E.description: Explain how evidence from technological advances supports or refutes the genetic relationships among groups of organisms (e.g., DNA analysis, protein analysis).

B6CAFCF0DFE601316E3168A86D17958E.description: Explain evolution in terms of how the Earth's present-day life forms evolved from earlier, distinctly different species as a consequence of the interactions of (1) the potential for a species to increase its numbers, (2) the genetic variability of offspring due to mutation and recombination of genes, (3) a finite supply of the resources required for life, and (4) the ensuing selection.

B6CA9E30DFE601316E3068A86D17958E.description: Explain the contributions of Darwin, Malthus, Wallace and Russell to the advancement of life science.

B6CA3220DFE601316E2F68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the abilities and behaviors an organism has, and likelihood of its survival strongly depend on its heritable characteristics, which can be biochemical and anatomical.

B6C9B180DFE601316E2E68A86D17958E.description: Explain the currently accepted theory for the development of life on Earth, including the history of its origin and the evolutionary process.

B6C8F5F0DFE601316E2C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the aspects of environmental protection, such as ecosystem protection, habitat management, species conservation and environmental agencies and regulations; and evaluate and justify the need for public policy in guiding the use and management of the environment.

B6C89EB0DFE601316E2B68A86D17958E.description: Identify ways of detecting, and limiting or reversing environmental damage.

B6C83E90DFE601316E2A68A86D17958E.description: Identify ways humans can impact and alter the stability of ecosystems, such as habitat destruction, pollution, and consumption of resources; and describe the potentially irreversible effects these changes can cause.

B6D17B20DFE601316E4268A86D17958E.description: Identify the factors in an ecosystem that can affect its carrying capacity.

B6D11330DFE601316E4168A86D17958E.description: Describe how the interrelationships and interdependencies among organisms generate stable ecosystems that fluctuate around a state of rough equilibrium for hundreds or thousands of years.

B6D0BE20DFE601316E4068A86D17958E.description: Explain how the amount of life an environment can sustain is restricted by the availability of matter and energy, and the ability of the ecosystem to recycle materials.

B6D01120DFE601316E3E68A86D17958E.description: Energy flows and matter recycles through an ecosystem.

B6C425F0DFE601316E1F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the structures of proteins and their role in cell function.

B6C3CF10DFE601316E1E68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the processes of photosynthesis and cellular respiration are interrelated and contribute to biogeochemical cycles.

B6C37800DFE601316E1D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize how an organism's organization and complexity accommodate its need for obtaining, transforming, transporting, releasing, and eliminating the matter and energy used to sustain it.

B6C31E30DFE601316E1C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize how cell functions are regulated through changes in the activity of the functions performed by proteins, and through the selective expression of individual genes; and explain how this regulation allows cells to respond to their environment and to control and coordinate cell growth and division.

B6C2BEF0DFE601316E1B68A86D17958E.description: Identify the structures of different types of cell parts/organelles and explain the functions they perform.

B6C1F830DFE601316E1968A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells according to general structure and degrees of complexity.

B6C1A0F0DFE601316E1868A86D17958E.description: Identify plants and animals according to binomial nomenclature.

B6C14F20DFE601316E1768A86D17958E.description: Explain that organisms that possess similar DNA code are more closely related than those in which DNA varies greatly.

B6C0FAF0DFE601316E1668A86D17958E.description: Describe how organisms are classified into a hierarchy of groups and subgroups, which are based on similarities that reflect their evolutionary relationships.

B6C04A00DFE601316E1468A86D17958E.description: All living organisms have identifiable structures and characteristics that allow for survival (organisms, populations, and species).

B6BFA550DFE601316E1268A86D17958E.description: Explain the kinds of applications of knowledge and skills necessary for jobs/careers specific to Earth or space sciences.

B6BEF610DFE601316E1068A86D17958E.description: Explain how the use of technologies at a local level, such as burning of fossil fuels for transportation or power generation, may contribute to global environmental problems.

B6BE9880DFE601316E0F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the means for transforming a natural material, such as iron ore, into useful products during different historical periods, such as the Stone Age, Iron Age, Renaissance, the Industrial Period and the current Age of Information.

B6BE45C0DFE601316E0E68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between and provide examples of renewable and nonrenewable sources of energy; and explain the advantages and limitations of each.

B6BD9510DFE601316E0C68A86D17958E.description: Explain how scientists study the Earth using computer-generated models and observations from both landbased sites and satellites; and describe the value of using these tools in unison.

B6BD30F0DFE601316E0B68A86D17958E.description: Describe the use and benefits of land-based light telescopes, radio telescopes, spectrophotometers, satellites, manned exploration, probes, and robots to the study of Earth Space Science.

B6BC5E00DFE601316E0968A86D17958E.description: Understand that technology is designed with a particular function in mind; and principles of Earth Space science are useful in creating technology for the Earth space sciences.

B6BC0550DFE601316E0868A86D17958E.description: Describe ways in which technology has increased our understanding of the universe.

B6BB57A0DFE601316E0668A86D17958E.description: The growth of scientific knowledge in Earth Space Science has been advanced through the development of technology and is used (alone or in combination with other sciences) to identify, understand and solve local and global issues.

B6BAF4E0DFE601316E0568A86D17958E.description: Explain how scientific theories about the structure of the universe have been advanced through the use of sophisticated technology (e.g., space probes and visual, radio and x-ray telescopes).

B6BA9C60DFE601316E0468A86D17958E.description: Based on the nature of electromagnetic waves, explain the movement and location of objects in the universe or their composition (e.g., red shift, blue shift, line spectra).

B6BA4510DFE601316E0368A86D17958E.description: Provide scientific evidence that supports or refutes the "Big Bang" theory of how the universe was formed.

B6B9ED80DFE601316E0268A86D17958E.description: Explain the evidence that suggests the universe is expanding.

B6B99170DFE601316E0168A86D17958E.description: Explain that current scientific evidence supports the Big Bang Theory as a probable explanation of the origin of the universe, and describe the theory.

B6B8DAF0DFE601316DFF68A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationships between or among the energy produced from nuclear reactions, the origin of elements, and the life cycles of stars.

B6B87BC0DFE601316DFE68A86D17958E.description: Describe the ongoing processes involved in star formation, their life cycles and their destruction.

B6B81BB0DFE601316DFD68A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the characteristics common to most stars in the universe.

B6B6F570DFE601316DFA68A86D17958E.description: Recognize electromagnetic waves can be used to locate objects in the universe, and track their movement.

B6B641B0DFE601316DF868A86D17958E.description: The origin and evolution of galaxies and the universe demonstrate fundamental principles of physical science across vast distances and time.

B6B5E590DFE601316DF768A86D17958E.description: Explain how the Solar System formed from a giant cloud of gas and debris about 5 billion years ago.

B6B58740DFE601316DF668A86D17958E.description: Explain how gravitational force influenced the formations of the planets and their moons; and describe how these objects move in patterns under its continued influence.

B6B4D5E0DFE601316DF468A86D17958E.description: Explain how internal and external sources of heat (energy) fuel geologic processes (e.g., rock cycle, plate tectonics, sea floor spreading).

B6B47C80DFE601316DF368A86D17958E.description: Explain how the inclination of incoming solar radiation can impact the amount of energy Earth receives on any given surface area.

B6B41FF0DFE601316DF268A86D17958E.description: Identify the Earth's major external source of energy as solar energy.

B6B36040DFE601316DF068A86D17958E.description: Explain how the Earth, Moon and Sun were formed.

B6B28820DFE601316DEE68A86D17958E.description: The Earth is part of a solar system, made up of distinct parts, which have temporal and spatial interrelationships.

B6B226F0DFE601316DED68A86D17958E.description: Explain that water quality can be affected positively or negatively by outside sources

B6B17850DFE601316DEB68A86D17958E.description: Explain that throughout the rock cycle, the total amount of the material remains the same.

B6B082D0DFE601316DE968A86D17958E.description: Explain how internal and external sources of heat (energy) fuel geologic processes (e.g., rock cycle, plate tectonics, sea floor spreading).

B6B025C0DFE601316DE868A86D17958E.description: Trace the development of the theory of plate tectonics.

B6AFD3C0DFE601316DE768A86D17958E.description: Provide supporting geologic/geographic evidence that supports the validity of the theory of plate tectonics.

B6AF81A0DFE601316DE668A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the major external and internal sources of energy on Earth.

B6AE0A10DFE601316DE268A86D17958E.description: Provided with geologic data (including movement of plates) on a given locale, predict the likelihood for an earth event (e.g. volcanoes mountain ranges, islands, earthquakes, tides, tsunamis).

B6AC3D60DFE601316DDD68A86D17958E.description: Describe the movement of crustal plates and explain how the effects have altered the Earth's features.

B6ABE2F0DFE601316DDC68A86D17958E.description: Explain the theory of plate tectonics.

B6AB78F0DFE601316DDB68A86D17958E.description: Describe the conditions that enable the Earth to support life, such as the availability of water, the gravitational force, the electromagnetic field and the intensity of radiation from the Sun.

B6AAFB00DFE601316DDA68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that elements exist in fixed amounts and describe how they move through the solid Earth, oceans, atmosphere, and living things as part of geochemical cycles, such as the water, carbon and nitrogen cycles.

B6AA4AE0DFE601316DD868A86D17958E.description: Explain how Earth's features can affect wind and weather patterns by causing air to rise and increasing precipitation.

B6A9F480DFE601316DD768A86D17958E.description: Describe how Earth's atmospheric composition has changed from the formation of the Earth through current time.

B6A99820DFE601316DD668A86D17958E.description: Explain how heat and energy transfer in and out of the atmosphere; and provide examples of how it is related to weather and climate.

B6A93140DFE601316DD568A86D17958E.description: Explain how winds and ocean currents are created on the Earth's surface.

B6A85860DFE601316DD368A86D17958E.description: The Earth and Earth materials, as we know them today, have developed over long periods of time, through constant change processes.

B6A36700DFE601316DC568A86D17958E.description: Use electronic networks to share information.

B6A31340DFE601316DC468A86D17958E.description: Prepare multimedia presentations to share results of investigations, demonstrating a clear sense of audience and purpose.

B6A19A60DFE601316DC068A86D17958E.description: Formulate scientific questions about an issue and define experimental procedures for finding answers.

B6A0CAC0DFE601316DBE68A86D17958E.description: Apply scientific knowledge and skills to make reasoned decisions about the use of science and scientific innovations.

B6A072A0DFE601316DBD68A86D17958E.description: Generate solutions to scientific questions and challenges through developing, modeling and revising investigations.

B6A01480DFE601316DBC68A86D17958E.description: Pursue scientific inquiry such as observation, measurement, hypothesis formation and analysis, and value "habits of mind" such as persistence, accuracy, and collaboration.

B69F0450DFE601316DB968A86D17958E.description: Create written reports and journals to share and communicate scientific ideas, plans, results, and conclusions resulting from observations and investigations.

B690AA70DFE601316D9368A86D17958E.description: Understand that the basic idea of mathematical modeling is to find a mathematical relationship that behaves in the same way as the objects or processes under investigation; a mathematical model may give insight about how something really works or may fit observations very well without any intuitive meaning.

B68E6FA0DFE601316D8D68A86D17958E.description: Realize that in science, the testing, revising, and occasional discarding of theories, new and old, never ends; this ongoing process leads to an increasingly better understanding of how things work in the world but not to absolute truth.
