comments: of reading comprehension strategies might include: using prior knowledge; summarizing; predicting and making text based inferences; determining importance; generating literal, clarifying, inferential, analysis, synthesis, and evaluative questions; constructing sensory images (e.g., making pictures in one's mind); making connections (text to self, text to text, and text to world); taking notes; locating and using text discourse features and elements to support inferences and generalizations about information (e.g., vocabulary, text structure, evidence, format, use of language, arguments used); or using cues for text structures (e.g., chronological, cause/effect, compare/contrast, proposition and support, description, classification, logical, sequential like Grade 10) (Local) (See also Appendix D)

B2724AC0DFE60131660268A86D17958E.description: Uses comprehension strategies (flexibly and as needed) before, during, and after reading literary and informational text. (Local)

B2720220DFE60131660168A86D17958E.description: Strategies for Monitoring and Adjusting and Reading Comprehension Strategies (RS:1), (RS:2)

B27166A0DFE6013165FF68A86D17958E.description: Evaluating the clarity and accuracy of information (e.g., consistency, effectiveness of organizational pattern, or logic of arguments) (Local)

B27120D0DFE6013165FE68A86D17958E.description: Making inferences about causes and effects (Local)

B270D480DFE6013165FD68A86D17958E.description: Critiquing author's use of strategies to achieve intended purpose or message (e.g., to inform, explain, entertain, persuade) (Local)
comments: (critique public documents): May include analysis of using anecdotes, addressing counterclaims, appealing to audience, using emotionally-laden language
(critique functional documents): May include visual appeal, logical sequences, awareness of possible reader misunderstanding

B27090A0DFE6013165FC68A86D17958E.description: Drawing inferences about text, including author's purpose (e.g., to inform, explain, entertain, persuade) or message; or explaining how purpose may affect the interpretation of the text; or using supporting evidence to form or evaluate opinions/judgments and assertions about central ideas that are relevant (Local)

B2704AB0DFE6013165FB68A86D17958E.description: Synthesizing and evaluating information within or across text(s) (e.g., constructing appropriate titles; or formulating assertions or controlling ideas) (Local)

B27002B0DFE6013165FA68A86D17958E.description: Explaining connections among ideas across multiple texts (Local)

B26FBAD0DFE6013165F968A86D17958E.description: Analyze and interpret informational text (which may include technical writing), citing evidence as appropriate by…

B26F74E0DFE6013165F868A86D17958E.description: Analysis and Interpretation of Informational Text (Expository and Practical Text across Content Areas) / Citing Evidence (IT:2)

B26F1C50DFE6013165F768A86D17958E.description: Identifying the characteristics of a variety of types of text (e.g., reference), public documents (drivers' manuals) and discourse, essays (including literary criticisms), articles, technical manuals, editorials/commentaries, primary source documents, periodicals, job-related materials, speeches, on-line reading, documentaries; and practical/functional procedures/instructions, announcements, invitations, book orders, recipes, menus, advertisements, pamphlets, schedules) (Local)

B26ED200DFE6013165F668A86D17958E.description: Generating questions before, during, and after reading to enhance understanding and recall; expand understanding and/or gain new information (Local)

B26E8480DFE6013165F568A86D17958E.description: Organizing information to show understanding or relationships among facts, ideas, and events (e.g., representing main/central ideas or details within text through charting (including flowcharts), mapping, paraphrasing, summarizing, comparing/contrasting, outlining, or connecting information with related ideas, etc.) (Local)

B26E4070DFE6013165F468A86D17958E.description: Using information from the text to answer questions, perform specific tasks, or solve problems; to state the main/central ideas; to provide supporting details; to explain visual components supporting the text; or to interpret maps, charts, timelines, tables, or diagrams (Local)

B26DFC70DFE6013165F368A86D17958E.description: Obtaining information from text features [e.g., table of contents, glossary, index, transition words/phrases, transitional devices (including use of white space), bold or italicized text, headings, subheadings, graphic organizers, charts, graphs, or illustrations] (Local)

B26DB290DFE6013165F268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate initial understanding of informational texts (expository and practical texts) by…

B26D6430DFE6013165F168A86D17958E.description: Initial Understanding of Informational Text (Expository and Practical Text across Content Areas) (IT:1)

B26CDD00DFE6013165EF68A86D17958E.description: Examining author's style or use of literary devices to convey theme (Local)

B26C9210DFE6013165EE68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrating knowledge of author's style or use of literary elements and devices (e.g., simile, metaphor, point of view, imagery, repetition, flashback, foreshadowing, personification, hyperbole, symbolism, analogize allusion, diction, syntax, genre, or bias, or use of punctuation, etc.) to analyze literary works (Local)

B26C4290DFE6013165ED68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and interpret author's craft within or across texts, citing evidence where appropriate by…

B26BEFA0DFE6013165EC68A86D17958E.description: Explaining how the author's purpose (e.g., to entertain, inform or persuade) message or theme (which may include universal themes) is supported within the text(s) (Local)

B26B9E30DFE6013165EB68A86D17958E.description: Explaining how the narrator's point of view, or author's style, or tone is evident and affects the reader's interpretation or is supported throughout the text(s) (Local)

B26B5800DFE6013165EA68A86D17958E.description: Making inferences about cause/effect, internal or external conflicts (e.g., person versus self, person versus person, person versus nature/society/fate), or the relationship among elements within text(s) (e.g., describing the interaction among plot/subplots, theme/setting, symbolism/characterization) (Local)

B26B0FD0DFE6013165E968A86D17958E.description: Examining characterization (e.g., stereotype, antagonist, protagonist), motivation, or interactions (including relationships), citing thoughts, words, or actions that reveal character traits, motivations, or changes over time (Local)

B26ACB40DFE6013165E868A86D17958E.description: Explaining and supporting logical predictions or logical outcomes (e.g., drawing conclusions based on interactions between characters or evolving plot) (Local)

B26A82A0DFE6013165E768A86D17958E.description: Analyze and interpret literary elements within or across texts, citing evidence where appropriate by…

B26A3380DFE6013165E668A86D17958E.description: Providing relevant details to support the connections made or judgments (interpretive, analytical, evaluative, or reflective) (Local)

B269D350DFE6013165E568A86D17958E.description: Comparing stories or other texts to related personal experience, prior knowledge, or to other books (Local)

B26981A0DFE6013165E468A86D17958E.description: Generates a personal response to what is read through a variety of means by…

B2693640DFE6013165E368A86D17958E.description: Analysis and Interpretation of Literary Text, Citing Evidence (LT:2), (LT:3), (LT:4)

B268F140DFE6013165E268A86D17958E.description: Identify literary devices as appropriate to genre (e.g., similes, metaphors, alliteration, rhyme scheme, onomatopoeia, imagery, repetition, flashback, foreshadowing, personification, hyperbole, symbolism, allusion, diction, syntax, bias, or point of view) (Local)

B2689CB0DFE6013165E168A86D17958E.description: Identifying the characteristics of a variety of types/genres of literary text (e.g., literary texts: poetry, plays, fairytales, fantasy, fables, realistic fiction, folktales, historical fiction, mysteries, science fiction, legends, myths, short stories, epics, novels, dramatic presentations, comedies, tragedies, satires, parodies, memoirs, epistles) (Local)

B2685420DFE6013165E068A86D17958E.description: Generating questions before, during, and after reading to enhance understanding and recall enhance/expand understanding and/or gaining new information (Local)

B26803A0DFE6013165DF68A86D17958E.description: Paraphrasing or summarizing key ideas/plot, with major events sequenced, as appropriate to text (Local)

B267C0C0DFE6013165DE68A86D17958E.description: Identifying, describing, or making logical predictions about character (such as protagonist or antagonist), setting, problem/solution, or plots/subplots, as appropriate to text; or identifying any significant changes in character, relationships, or setting over time; or identifying rising action, climax, or falling action (Local)

B2677D50DFE6013165DD68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate initial understanding of elements of literary texts by…

B2667CE0DFE6013165DA68A86D17958E.description: Selecting appropriate words or explaining the use of words in context, including connotation or denotation, shades of meanings of words/nuances, or idioms; or use of content-specific vocabulary, words with multiple meanings, precise language, or technical vocabulary (Local)

B2662AC0DFE6013165D968A86D17958E.description: Identifying synonyms, antonyms, homonyms/homophones, shades of meaning, analogies, idioms, or word origins, including words from dialects, or other languages that have been adopted into standard English (Local)

B265E9A0DFE6013165D868A86D17958E.description: Shows breadth of vocabulary knowledge through demonstrating understanding of word meanings and relationships by…

B2656950DFE6013165D668A86D17958E.description: Using strategies to unlock meaning including prior knowledge, base words, general and specialized print or electronic resources to determine definition, pronunciation, etymology, or usage of words (Local)

B2652540DFE6013165D568A86D17958E.description: Using strategies to unlock meaning (e.g., prior knowledge of word structure, including prefixes/suffixes, common roots, or word origins; or context clues; or resources including dictionaries, glossaries, or thesauruses to determine definition, pronunciation, etymology, or usage of words) (Local)

B264D9B0DFE6013165D468A86D17958E.description: Students identify the meaning of unfamiliar vocabulary by…

B26405A0DFE6013165D168A86D17958E.description: Identifying multi-syllabic words by using knowledge of sounds, syllable division, and word patterns (Local)

B262E7E0DFE6013165CD68A86D17958E.description: Fluency: reading familiar text with phrasing and expression, and with attention to text features such as punctuation, italics, and dialogue (Local)

B262A200DFE6013165CC68A86D17958E.description: Fluency: reading with appropriate silent and oral reading fluency rates as determined by text demands, and purpose for reading (Local)

B2625D70DFE6013165CB68A86D17958E.description: Accuracy: reading material appropriate for high school with at least 90-94% accuracy (Local)

document.title: K-12 Science Literacy New Hampshire Curriculum Framework

B7A9AF30DFE60131700D68A86D17958E.description: Understand the various scientific fields that use scientific content and skills and distinguish between professional and skilled science jobs/careers in the physical sciences.

B7A94E40DFE60131700C68A86D17958E.description: Explain the kinds of applications of knowledge and skills necessary for jobs/careers specific to the physical sciences.

B7A89850DFE60131700A68A86D17958E.description: Understand that a manufacturing system includes design of the product and methods of obtaining raw materials, as well as actual production, marketing, sales, maintenance, servicing, repair, and final disposal of the remains of the product.

B7A82EE0DFE60131700968A86D17958E.description: Describe the various types of manufacturing systems, such as customized production, batch production, and continuous production, and explain that manufacturing results in two types of good, durable and non-durable goods.

B7A7C3D0DFE60131700868A86D17958E.description: Design a transportation system that meets most humans' need for reliable and affordable transportation, while having a minimal impact on the environment.

B7A74280DFE60131700768A86D17958E.description: Compare two different energy systems that are used to produce large amounts of electrical power for New Hampshire residents, and describe the advantages and disadvantages of each system.

B7A6E5C0DFE60131700668A86D17958E.description: Explain the benefits of standardization of parts.

B7A67D90DFE60131700568A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship between energy and power.

B7A603C0DFE60131700468A86D17958E.description: Calculate the efficiency of an engine, and explain why a perfectly efficient engine is impossible.

B7A59E20DFE60131700368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate and explain how an engine converts chemical energy in the form of fuel, into mechanical energy in the form of motion.

B7A54520DFE60131700268A86D17958E.description: Explain that power systems have a source of energy, a process, loads, and some have a feedback system.

B7A4E690DFE60131700168A86D17958E.description: Social Issues (Local and Global) Energy, Power, and Transportation Manufacturing

B7A48AD0DFE60131700068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the appropriate use of a variety of input devices, such as scanners, voice/sound recorders, and digital cameras.

B7A42B10DFE601316FFF68A86D17958E.description: Identify tools, such as thermostats and thermal sensors, and explain their use in environmental control systems.

B7A35E80DFE601316FFD68A86D17958E.description: Relate the transfer of energy through conduction, convection and radiation to design technologies.

B7A2E490DFE601316FFC68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the basic principles of energy, work and power are related to design technology.

B7A21530DFE601316FFA68A86D17958E.description: The growth of scientific knowledge in Physical Science has been advanced through the development of technology and is used (alone or in combination with other sciences) to identify, understand and solve local and global issues.

B7A1AC70DFE601316FF968A86D17958E.description: Describe the predictions made by the theory of general relativity, and the evidence that supports it.

B7A14EF0DFE601316FF868A86D17958E.description: Understand the basic idea behind the theory of general relativity.

B7A0E9F0DFE601316FF768A86D17958E.description: Explain general concepts related to the theory of special relativity: time dilation, length contraction, and mass expansion.

B7A05FD0DFE601316FF668A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects on wavelength and frequency as electromagnetic waves interact with matter (e.g., light diffraction, blue sky).

B79FC680DFE601316FF568A86D17958E.description: Apply the concepts of inertia, motion, and momentum to predict and explain situations involving forces and motion, including stationary objects and collisions.

B79F6BF0DFE601316FF468A86D17958E.description: Recognize that apparent changes in wavelength can provide information about changes in motion; explain that the observed wavelength of a wave depends upon the relative motion of the source and the observer; and relate these to the differences between shorter and longer wavelengths.

B79F10C0DFE601316FF368A86D17958E.description: Interpret and apply the laws of motion to determine the effects of forces on the motion of objects.

B79E5030DFE601316FF168A86D17958E.description: Understand the basic principles of unified field theories.

B79DE110DFE601316FF068A86D17958E.description: Describe the gauge particles that are exchanged by each of the fundamental forces.

B79D78F0DFE601316FEF68A86D17958E.description: Understand the four fundamental forces found in nature: gravitation, electromagnetism, strong nuclear force, and weak nuclear force.

B79D16C0DFE601316FEE68A86D17958E.description: Given information (e.g., graphs, data, diagrams), use the relationships between or among force, mass, velocity, momentum, and acceleration to predict and explain the motion of objects.

B79CB5B0DFE601316FED68A86D17958E.description: Describe the difference between materials that contain equal proportions of positive and negative charges and those that have a very small excess or deficit of negative charges.

B79C58B0DFE601316FEC68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that different kinds of materials respond to electric forces in various ways; and differentiate between insulators, semiconductors, conductors and superconductors.

B79BF830DFE601316FEB68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that electromagnetic forces exist within and between atoms.

B79B9DB0DFE601316FEA68A86D17958E.description: Compare the strength of nuclear, electromagnetic and gravitational forces; and explain that the strength of nuclear forces account for the great amounts of energy released from the nuclear reactions in atomic or hydrogen bombs, and in the Sun and other stars.

B79B3A70DFE601316FE968A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the strength of the gravitational force between two masses is proportional to the masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

B79AC570DFE601316FE868A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the strength of the electric force between two charged objects is proportional to the charges and, as with gravitation, is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

B79A6A80DFE601316FE768A86D17958E.description: Explain that magnetic forces are related to the action of electrons and can be thought of as different aspects of a single electromagnetic force; and describe how the interplay of these forces is the basis for electric motors, generators, radio, television, and many other modern technologies.

B799B6D0DFE601316FE568A86D17958E.description: The motion of an object is affected by force.

B7995EB0DFE601316FE468A86D17958E.description: Understand that activation energy is required to make a chemical reaction proceed, whether or not it is exothermic or endothermic.

B798A960DFE601316FE268A86D17958E.description: Using information provided about chemical changes, draw conclusions about the energy flow in a given chemical reaction (e.g., exothermic reactions, endothermic reactions).

B7983560DFE601316FE168A86D17958E.description: Describe how electrons flow easily in some materials, such as metals, whereas in insulating materials, such as glass, they can hardly flow at all.

B797DAA0DFE601316FE068A86D17958E.description: Explain that nuclear reactions convert a fraction of the mass of interacting particles into energy and release much greater amounts of energy than atomic interactions.

B7977CA0DFE601316FDF68A86D17958E.description: Explain that waves, such as light, seismic, sound waves, have energy and can transfer energy when they interact with matter.

B7971F50DFE601316FDE68A86D17958E.description: Describe the relationship between heat and temperature, explaining that heat energy consists of the random motion and vibrations of atoms, molecules, and ions; and that the higher the temperature, the greater the atomic or molecular motion.

B796BB40DFE601316FDD68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the human eye can only see a narrow range of wavelengths within the electromagnetic spectrum; and explain how the variations of wavelength within that range of visible light are perceived as differences in color.

B7965B00DFE601316FDC68A86D17958E.description: Explain the range of the electromagnetic spectrum as it relates to both wavelength and energy; and provide examples of practical applications of the different wavelengths in the spectrum.

B795F4D0DFE601316FDB68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the energy associated with individual atoms and molecules can be used to identify the substances they comprise; and explain that each kind of atom or molecule can gain or lose energy only in particular discrete amounts, absorbing and emitting light only at wavelengths corresponding to these amounts.

B7957690DFE601316FDA68A86D17958E.description: Provide examples of how kinetic and potential energy can be transformed from one to the other.

B7950CE0DFE601316FD968A86D17958E.description: Explain that all energy can be considered to be either kinetic energy, potential energy, or energy contained by a field.

B7945450DFE601316FD768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how transformations of energy produce some energy in the form of heat and therefore the efficiency of the system is reduced (chemical, biological, and physical systems).

B793FD50DFE601316FD668A86D17958E.description: Identify the variety of structures that may be formed from the bonding of carbon atoms, and describe their roles in various chemical reactions, including those required for life processes.

B793A4E0DFE601316FD568A86D17958E.description: Recognize that a large number of important reactions involve the transfer of either electrons or hydrogen ions between reacting ions, molecules, or atoms.

B7934370DFE601316FD468A86D17958E.description: Explain that chemical reactions can be accelerated by catalysts, such as enzymes.

B792E1F0DFE601316FD368A86D17958E.description: Explain that chemical reactions either release or consume energy.

B79234A0DFE601316FD168A86D17958E.description: Explain the complete mole concept and identify ways in which it can be used, such as to differentiate between actual and relative mass.

B791D860DFE601316FD068A86D17958E.description: Explain relationships between and among electric charges, magnetic fields, electromagnetic forces, and atomic particles.

B7917510DFE601316FCF68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the rates of chemical reactions can vary greatly; and identify the factors that influence these reaction rates, such as how often the reacting atoms and molecules encounter one another, the temperature, and the properties of the reacting species, including shape.

B790FA00DFE601316FCE68A86D17958E.description: Explain that compounds are formed through both ionic and covalent bonding.

B79093E0DFE601316FCD68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that atoms interact with one another by transferring or sharing electrons that are furthest from the nucleus; and explain that the outer electrons govern the chemical properties of an element.

B7902E80DFE601316FCC68A86D17958E.description: Recognize and explain that atoms may be bonded together into molecules or formula units (crystalline solids).

B78F2B40DFE601316FCA68A86D17958E.description: Energy is necessary for change to occur in matter. Energy can be stored, transferred and transformed, but cannot be destroyed.

B78ED5A0DFE601316FC968A86D17958E.description: Explain how properties of elements and the location of elements on the periodic table are related.

B78E7F70DFE601316FC868A86D17958E.description: Use physical and chemical properties as determined through an investigation to identify a substance.

B78E2480DFE601316FC768A86D17958E.description: Explain that states of matter rely on the arrangement and motion of molecules; and differentiate between the structures of solids, liquids, and gases.

B78DC730DFE601316FC668A86D17958E.description: Explain that radioactive materials are unstable and undergo spontaneous nuclear reactions, which emit particles and/or wavelike radiation.

B78D63F0DFE601316FC568A86D17958E.description: Explain how the chemical properties of an element are governed by the electron configuration of atoms, and describe how atoms interact with one another by transferring or sharing the outermost electrons.

B78D0BE0DFE601316FC468A86D17958E.description: Determine whether an atom is either electrically neutral or an ion by referring to its number of electrons.

B78CB180DFE601316FC368A86D17958E.description: Explain that the physical properties of a compound are determined by its molecular structure and the interactions among the molecules.

B78BEA50DFE601316FC168A86D17958E.description: Identify the sub-orbital shapes and geometric orientations of the orbitals electrons can occupy in atoms.

B78B7970DFE601316FC068A86D17958E.description: Recognize the main ideas of string theory.

B78B1A10DFE601316FBF68A86D17958E.description: Understand the basic building blocks of matter are quarks and leptons.

B78AC2C0DFE601316FBE68A86D17958E.description: Model and explain the structure of an atom or explain how an atom's electron configuration, particularly the outermost electron(s), determines how that atom can interact with other atoms.

B78A6910DFE601316FBD68A86D17958E.description: Scientific thought about atoms has changed over time. Using information (narratives or models of atoms) provided, cite evidence that changed our understanding of the atom and the development of atomic theory.

B78A0610DFE601316FBC68A86D17958E.description: Define isotopes; recognize that most elements have two or more isotopes; and explain that although the number of neutrons has little affect on how the atom interacts with others, they do affect the mass and stability of the nucleus.

B7897FE0DFE601316FBB68A86D17958E.description: Explain that neutrons and protons are made up of even smaller constituents.

B7892060DFE601316FBA68A86D17958E.description: Recognize how elements are arranged in the periodic table; and explain how this arrangement illustrates the repeating patterns among elements with similar properties, such as the relationship between atomic number and atomic mass.

B788C4E0DFE601316FB968A86D17958E.description: Recognize and describe the structure of an atom and explain how the major components interact with one another.

B7880900DFE601316FB768A86D17958E.description: All living and nonliving things are composed of matter having characteristic properties that distinguish one substance from another (independent of size/amount of substance).

B7874570DFE601316FB568A86D17958E.description: Understand the various scientific fields that use scientific content and skills; and distinguish between professional and skilled science jobs/careers in the life sciences.

B786E220DFE601316FB468A86D17958E.description: Explain the kinds of applications of knowledge and skills necessary for jobs/careers specific to the life sciences.

B78618A0DFE601316FB268A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate a biotechnology system in New Hampshire that focuses on a specific goal, such as pharmaceutical development; and describe all elements of the system, identifying the costs and the benefits.

B785BA20DFE601316FB168A86D17958E.description: Summarize arguments on both sides of a medical research controversy, such as stem cell research, cloning, or zootransplanation.

B7856470DFE601316FB068A86D17958E.description: Explain how genetic engineering is used to modify the DNA structure of an organism; and describe how this process is used to research and develop medically useful products, such as insulin.

B7850CD0DFE601316FAF68A86D17958E.description: Explain how advances in agriculture made using biotechnology have directly affected the food production over the past 100 years; and that this change has profoundly affected societies all over the globe, making larger populations and urban centers a possibility.

B784B260DFE601316FAE68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that biotechnology is used in many areas, such as agriculture, pharmaceuticals, the environment, and genetic engineering; and understand that it requires extensive knowledge of the systems being changed.

B7844D50DFE601316FAD68A86D17958E.description: Describe aspects of the medical system available to help people in New Hampshire, including: prevention programs, vaccines and pharmaceuticals, hospitals and rehabilitation facilities.

B783B5B0DFE601316FAC68A86D17958E.description: Describe ways technology can support and improve our understanding of environmental issues.

B7834D00DFE601316FAB68A86D17958E.description: Social Issues (Local And Global) Medical Technology and Biotechnology

B782E900DFE601316FAA68A86D17958E.description: Describe the use and benefits of equipment such as light microscopes, transmission electron microscopes, scanning electron microscopes, spectrophotometers, probes, and robotics to the study of the life sciences.

B7822BE0DFE601316FA868A86D17958E.description: Recognize the importance of technology as it relates to science, for purposes such as: access to information about living systems, medical diagnosis, sample collection and treatment, measurement, data collection, and storage, computation, and communication of information.

B781AFB0DFE601316FA768A86D17958E.description: Understand that technology is designed with a particular function in mind, and principles of life science are useful in creating technology for the life sciences.

B78138C0DFE601316FA668A86D17958E.description: Describe ways in which technology has increased our understanding of the life sciences.

B7808380DFE601316FA468A86D17958E.description: The growth of scientific knowledge in Life Science has been advanced through the development of technology and is used (alone or in combination with other sciences) to identify, understand and solve local and global issues.

B78022D0DFE601316FA368A86D17958E.description: Explain how the immune system, endocrine system, or nervous system works and draw conclusions about how systems interact to maintain homeostasis in the human body.

B77FC900DFE601316FA268A86D17958E.description: Explain how the immune system functions to prevent and fight disease.

B77F6FE0DFE601316FA168A86D17958E.description: Describe how the length and quality of human life are influenced by many factors, including sanitation, diet, medical care, gender, genes, and environmental conditions and personal health behaviors.

B77EBC80DFE601316F9F68A86D17958E.description: Use evidence to make and support conclusions about the ways that humans or other organisms are affected by environmental factors or heredity (e.g., pathogens, diseases, medical advances, pollution, mutations).

B77E4420DFE601316F9E68A86D17958E.description: Explain that gene mutation in a cell can result in uncontrolled division, which is called cancer; and describe how exposure of cells to certain chemicals and radiation increase mutation, and thus the chance for cancer.

B77DD5A0DFE601316F9D68A86D17958E.description: Describe how some drugs mimic or block the molecules involved in transmitting nerve or hormone signals and explain how this disturbs the normal operations of the brain and body.

B77D7FC0DFE601316F9C68A86D17958E.description: Describe and provide examples of how new medical techniques, efficient health care delivery systems, improved sanitation, and a more complete understanding of the nature of disease provides today's humans a better chance of staying healthier than their forebears.

B77D2780DFE601316F9B68A86D17958E.description: Explain that vaccines were developed to reduce or eliminate diseases; and provide examples of how these medical advances have proven to be successful.

B77CC9A0DFE601316F9A68A86D17958E.description: Explain that disease in organisms can be caused by intrinsic failures of the system or infection by other organisms, and describe as well as provide examples of how some diseases are caused by: the breakdown in cellular function, congenital conditions, genetic disorders, malnutrition, and emotional health, including stress.

B77C0A90DFE601316F9868A86D17958E.description: Describe how the functions of all the human body systems are interrelated at a chemical level and how they maintain homeostasis.

B77BB490DFE601316F9768A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the immune system, endocrine system, and nervous system can affect the homeostasis of an organism.

B77B0210DFE601316F9568A86D17958E.description: Humans are similar to other species in many ways, and yet are unique among Earth's life forms.

B7758170DFE601316F8768A86D17958E.description: Understand the types of mutations that cause changes in DNA and cause the appearance of new alleles, such as frameshift and point mutations, and the chromosomal mutations of insertion, deletion, translocation, and duplication.

B7752000DFE601316F8668A86D17958E.description: Given a scenario, provide evidence that demonstrates how sexual reproduction results in a great variety of possible gene combinations and contributes to natural selection (e.g., Darwin's finches, isolation of a species, Tay Sach's disease).

B774AD50DFE601316F8568A86D17958E.description: Use pedigree charts and Punnet Squares to determine patterns of inheritance.

B7744880DFE601316F8468A86D17958E.description: Explain the concepts of Mendelian genetics.

B773EB60DFE601316F8368A86D17958E.description: Explain that gene mutations and new combinations may have a variety of effects on the organism, including positive and negative ones, or none at all.

B7739230DFE601316F8268A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe ways genes may be changed and combined to create genetic variation within a species.

B7732F10DFE601316F8168A86D17958E.description: Analyze present day data and research in areas, including antibiotic resistance in bacteria, changes in viral genomes, such as bird flu, and DNA sequencing; and relate it to the concepts of natural selection.

B7729C10DFE601316F8068A86D17958E.description: Recognize how a species' chance of survival increases with each variation of an organism within the species; and explain how, in the event of a major global change, the greater the diversity of species on Earth, the greater the chance for survival of life.

B7722D70DFE601316F7F68A86D17958E.description: Explain the diversity and unity of past and present life forms on Earth using currently accepted theories.

B771D010DFE601316F7E68A86D17958E.description: Explain the concept of natural selection.

B7711070DFE601316F7C68A86D17958E.description: Given information about living or extinct organisms, cite evidence to explain the frequency of inherited characteristics of organisms in a population; or explain the evolution of varied structures (with defined functions) that affected the organisms' survival in a specific environment (e.g., giraffe, wind pollination of flowers).

B770B990DFE601316F7B68A86D17958E.description: Explain how evidence from technological advances supports or refutes the genetic relationships among groups of organisms (e.g., DNA analysis, protein analysis).

B7705D20DFE601316F7A68A86D17958E.description: Explain evolution in terms of how the Earth's present-day life forms evolved from earlier, distinctly different species as a consequence of the interactions of (1) the potential for a species to increase its numbers, (2) the genetic variability of offspring due to mutation and recombination of genes, (3) a finite supply of the resources required for life, and (4) the ensuing selection.

B76FF550DFE601316F7968A86D17958E.description: Explain the contributions of Darwin, Malthus, Wallace and Russell to the advancement of life science.

B76F84A0DFE601316F7868A86D17958E.description: Recognize that the abilities and behaviors an organism has, and likelihood of its survival strongly depend on its heritable characteristics, which can be biochemical and anatomical.

B76F10E0DFE601316F7768A86D17958E.description: Explain the currently accepted theory for the development of life on Earth, including the history of its origin and the evolutionary process.

B76E6260DFE601316F7568A86D17958E.description: Analyze the aspects of environmental protection, such as ecosystem protection, habitat management, species conservation and environmental agencies and regulations; and evaluate and justify the need for public policy in guiding the use and management of the environment.

B76E0880DFE601316F7468A86D17958E.description: Identify ways of detecting, and limiting or reversing environmental damage.

B76DA8F0DFE601316F7368A86D17958E.description: Identify ways humans can impact and alter the stability of ecosystems, such as habitat destruction, pollution, and consumption of resources; and describe the potentially irreversible effects these changes can cause.

B76CDDE0DFE601316F7168A86D17958E.description: Groups of organisms show evidence of change over time (e.g. evolution, natural selection, structures, behaviors, and biochemistry).

B77A9B80DFE601316F9468A86D17958E.description: Trace the cycling of matter (e.g., carbon cycle) and the flow of energy in a living system from its source through its transformation in cellular, biochemical processes (e.g., photosynthesis, cellular respiration, fermentation).

B77A3A50DFE601316F9368A86D17958E.description: Explain that as matter and energy flow through different levels of organization in living systems and between living systems and the environment, elements, such as carbon and nitrogen, are recombined in different ways.

B77966A0DFE601316F9168A86D17958E.description: Use examples from local ecosystems to describe the relationships among organisms at the different trophic levels.

B7787EB0DFE601316F8F68A86D17958E.description: Explain or evaluate potential bias in how evidence is interpreted in reports concerning a particular environmental factor that impacts the biology of humans.

B7781BA0DFE601316F8E68A86D17958E.description: Using data from a specific ecosystem, explain relationships or make predictions about how environmental disturbance (human impact or natural events) affects the flow of energy or cycling of matter in an ecosystem.

B777BEA0DFE601316F8D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and describe how environmental disturbances, such as climate changes, natural events, human activity and the introduction of invasive species, can affect the flow of energy or matter in an ecosystem.

B7775E30DFE601316F8C68A86D17958E.description: Identify the factors in an ecosystem that can affect its carrying capacity.

B776FE40DFE601316F8B68A86D17958E.description: Describe how the interrelationships and interdependencies among organisms generate stable ecosystems that fluctuate around a state of rough equilibrium for hundreds or thousands of years.

B7769680DFE601316F8A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the amount of life an environment can sustain is restricted by the availability of matter and energy, and the ability of the ecosystem to recycle materials.

B775DEE0DFE601316F8868A86D17958E.description: Energy flows and matter recycles through an ecosystem.

B76C8170DFE601316F7068A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast the alternation of generations' life cycles; and understand the variations of the haploid and diploid phases that produce diplontic, haplontic, and isomorphic alternation of generations in living organisms.

B76C22D0DFE601316F6F68A86D17958E.description: Explain or justify with evidence how the alteration of the DNA sequence may produce new gene combinations that make little difference, enhance capabilities, or can be harmful to the organism (e.g., selective breeding, genetic engineering, mutations).

B76BC3B0DFE601316F6E68A86D17958E.description: Describe the alternation of generations, life cycles with haploid and diploid phases in living organisms, such as bacteria, plants and animals.

B76B69D0DFE601316F6D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that new heritable characteristics can only result from new combinations of existing genes or from mutations of genes in an organism's sex cells; and explain why other changes in an organism cannot be passed on.

B76B0370DFE601316F6C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the chemical and structural properties of DNA and explain its role in identifying the characteristics of an organism.

B76A1570DFE601316F6A68A86D17958E.description: Explain the process of cell differentiation, using stem cells as an example.

B769A7B0DFE601316F6968A86D17958E.description: Compare the processes of mitosis and meiosis, including disruptions to the cycles, such as disease or cancer.

B7694D10DFE601316F6868A86D17958E.description: Use data and observation to make connections between, to explain, or to justify how specific cell organelles produce/regulate what the cell needs or what a unicellular or multi-cellular organism needs for survival (e.g., protein synthesis, DNA transport, nerve cells).

B768F0D0DFE601316F6768A86D17958E.description: Recognize that because all matter tends toward more disorganized states, living systems need a continuous input of energy to maintain their chemical and physical organizations.

B7689460DFE601316F6668A86D17958E.description: Describe the chemical reactions involved in cell functions using examples from the nervous, immune and endocrine systems in multicellular animals.

B7683450DFE601316F6568A86D17958E.description: Describe the structures of proteins and their role in cell function.

B767CBF0DFE601316F6468A86D17958E.description: Explain how the processes of photosynthesis and cellular respiration are interrelated and contribute to biogeochemical cycles.

B76749B0DFE601316F6368A86D17958E.description: Recognize how an organism's organization and complexity accommodate its need for obtaining, transforming, transporting, releasing, and eliminating the matter and energy used to sustain it.

B766D4C0DFE601316F6268A86D17958E.description: Recognize how cell functions are regulated through changes in the activity of the functions performed by proteins, and through the selective expression of individual genes; and explain how this regulation allows cells to respond to their environment and to control and coordinate cell growth and division.

B7667720DFE601316F6168A86D17958E.description: Identify the structures of different types of cell parts/organelles and explain the functions they perform.

B765BB50DFE601316F5F68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells at the biochemical level, using cell wall composition, DNA structure, and other biochemical pathways.

B7655E80DFE601316F5E68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells according to general structure and degrees of complexity.

B764FF50DFE601316F5D68A86D17958E.description: Identify plants and animals according to binomial nomenclature.

B7649FB0DFE601316F5C68A86D17958E.description: Explain that organisms that possess similar DNA code are more closely related than those in which DNA varies greatly.

B76439B0DFE601316F5B68A86D17958E.description: Describe how organisms are classified into a hierarchy of groups and subgroups, which are based on similarities that reflect their evolutionary relationships.

B7637AD0DFE601316F5968A86D17958E.description: All living organisms have identifiable structures and characteristics that allow for survival (organisms, populations, and species).

B762A050DFE601316F5768A86D17958E.description: Understand the various scientific fields that use scientific content and skills; and distinguish between professional and skilled science jobs/careers in Earth or space sciences.

B7623630DFE601316F5668A86D17958E.description: Explain the kinds of applications of knowledge and skills necessary for jobs/careers specific to Earth or space sciences.

B76140A0DFE601316F5468A86D17958E.description: Research and evaluate a current environmental issue within the State of New Hampshire, such as a dispute regarding the conversion of a natural environment to human use; and construct a defense that supports environmental protection.

B760E190DFE601316F5368A86D17958E.description: Provide examples of how man's use of Earth materials has changed over time; and use those examples to explain how the relationship between science and technology has gradually grown closer in the past century.

B76079A0DFE601316F5268A86D17958E.description: Explain the environmental effects of using both renewable and nonrenewable resources; and provide examples of how man is addressing these effects on the environment.

B7601B90DFE601316F5168A86D17958E.description: Explain how the use of technologies at a local level, such as burning of fossil fuels for transportation or power generation, may contribute to global environmental problems.

B75FB5C0DFE601316F5068A86D17958E.description: Describe the means for transforming a natural material, such as iron ore, into useful products during different historical periods, such as the Stone Age, Iron Age, Renaissance, the Industrial Period and the current Age of Information.

B75F5910DFE601316F4F68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between and provide examples of renewable and nonrenewable sources of energy; and explain the advantages and limitations of each.

B75E9350DFE601316F4D68A86D17958E.description: Explain how scientists study the Earth using computer-generated models and observations from both landbased sites and satellites; and describe the value of using these tools in unison.

B75E2D90DFE601316F4C68A86D17958E.description: Describe the use and benefits of land-based light telescopes, radio telescopes, spectrophotometers, satellites, manned exploration, probes, and robots to the study of Earth Space Science.

B75D5C60DFE601316F4A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize the importance of technology as it relates to science, for purposes such as: access to space and other remote locations, sample collection and treatment, measurement, data collection, and storage, computation, and communication of information.

B75CF550DFE601316F4968A86D17958E.description: Understand that technology is designed with a particular function in mind; and principles of Earth Space science are useful in creating technology for the Earth space sciences.

B75C95A0DFE601316F4868A86D17958E.description: Describe ways in which technology has increased our understanding of the universe.

B75BCAC0DFE601316F4668A86D17958E.description: The growth of scientific knowledge in Earth Space Science has been advanced through the development of technology and is used (alone or in combination with other sciences) to identify, understand and solve local and global issues.

B75B65C0DFE601316F4568A86D17958E.description: Explain how scientific theories about the structure of the universe have been advanced through the use of sophisticated technology (e.g., space probes and visual, radio and x-ray telescopes).

B75B01A0DFE601316F4468A86D17958E.description: Based on the nature of electromagnetic waves, explain the movement and location of objects in the universe or their composition (e.g., red shift, blue shift, line spectra).

B75AAA10DFE601316F4368A86D17958E.description: Provide scientific evidence that supports or refutes the "Big Bang" theory of how the universe was formed.

B75A5280DFE601316F4268A86D17958E.description: Explain the evidence that suggests the universe is expanding.

B759F940DFE601316F4168A86D17958E.description: Explain that current scientific evidence supports the Big Bang Theory as a probable explanation of the origin of the universe, and describe the theory.

B7593330DFE601316F3F68A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationships between or among the energy produced from nuclear reactions, the origin of elements, and the life cycles of stars.

B758CFF0DFE601316F3E68A86D17958E.description: Describe the ongoing processes involved in star formation, their life cycles and their destruction.

B7586B00DFE601316F3D68A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the characteristics common to most stars in the universe.

B7574AA0DFE601316F3A68A86D17958E.description: Recognize electromagnetic waves can be used to locate objects in the universe, and track their movement.

B7568A10DFE601316F3868A86D17958E.description: The origin and evolution of galaxies and the universe demonstrate fundamental principles of physical science across vast distances and time.

B75601D0DFE601316F3768A86D17958E.description: Explain how the Solar System formed from a giant cloud of gas and debris about 5 billion years ago.

B7559550DFE601316F3668A86D17958E.description: Explain how gravitational force influenced the formations of the planets and their moons; and describe how these objects move in patterns under its continued influence.

B754E150DFE601316F3468A86D17958E.description: Explain how internal and external sources of heat (energy) fuel geologic processes (e.g., rock cycle, plate tectonics, sea floor spreading).

B7547B70DFE601316F3368A86D17958E.description: Explain how the inclination of incoming solar radiation can impact the amount of energy Earth receives on any given surface area.

B7541310DFE601316F3268A86D17958E.description: Identify the Earth's major external source of energy as solar energy.

B7533480DFE601316F3068A86D17958E.description: Understand how the Nebular Hypothesis, fusion, and the process of differentiation contributes to the structure and organization of the universe.

B752D960DFE601316F2F68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the Earth, Moon and Sun were formed.

B7522020DFE601316F2D68A86D17958E.description: The Earth is part of a solar system, made up of distinct parts, which have temporal and spatial interrelationships.

B751BEF0DFE601316F2C68A86D17958E.description: Explain that water quality can be affected positively or negatively by outside sources

B75108E0DFE601316F2A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the various types of igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks found on Earth.

B7509FF0DFE601316F2968A86D17958E.description: Describe the processes that transform one type of rock into another, such as lithification, metamorphosis, and weathering on a chemical level.

B7503E50DFE601316F2868A86D17958E.description: Explain that throughout the rock cycle, the total amount of the material remains the same.

B74F7F40DFE601316F2668A86D17958E.description: Explain how internal and external sources of heat (energy) fuel geologic processes (e.g., rock cycle, plate tectonics, sea floor spreading).

B74F24B0DFE601316F2568A86D17958E.description: Trace the development of the theory of plate tectonics.

B74ECB60DFE601316F2468A86D17958E.description: Provide supporting geologic/geographic evidence that supports the validity of the theory of plate tectonics.

B74E6C40DFE601316F2368A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the major external and internal sources of energy on Earth.

B74E0550DFE601316F2268A86D17958E.description: Relate plate movement to earthquakes and volcanic activity, and explain how it results in tectonic uplift and mountain building.

B74DABB0DFE601316F2168A86D17958E.description: Explain that the Earth is composed of interactive layers, which have distinct compositions, physical properties and processes.

B74CF940DFE601316F1F68A86D17958E.description: Provided with geologic data (including movement of plates) on a given locale, predict the likelihood for an earth event (e.g. volcanoes mountain ranges, islands, earthquakes, tides, tsunamis).

B74C9D00DFE601316F1E68A86D17958E.description: Observation Of The Earth From Space

B74C2990DFE601316F1D68A86D17958E.description: Relate how geologic time is determined using various dating methods (e.g., radioactive decay, rock sequences, fossil records).

B74BB910DFE601316F1C68A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the methods used to measure geologic time, such as fossil identification, radioactive dating, and rock sequences.

B74ACA70DFE601316F1A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the movement of crustal plates and explain how the effects have altered the Earth's features.

B74A61C0DFE601316F1968A86D17958E.description: Explain the theory of plate tectonics.

B74A0830DFE601316F1868A86D17958E.description: Describe the conditions that enable the Earth to support life, such as the availability of water, the gravitational force, the electromagnetic field and the intensity of radiation from the Sun.

B749AEB0DFE601316F1768A86D17958E.description: Recognize that elements exist in fixed amounts and describe how they move through the solid Earth, oceans, atmosphere, and living things as part of geochemical cycles, such as the water, carbon and nitrogen cycles.

B748F660DFE601316F1568A86D17958E.description: Understand the effects of solar influences, such as flares and sunspots, on atmospheric conditions.

B7488A90DFE601316F1468A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe the layers of the atmosphere.

B7483360DFE601316F1368A86D17958E.description: Explain how Earth's features can affect wind and weather patterns by causing air to rise and increasing precipitation.

B747DB30DFE601316F1268A86D17958E.description: Describe how Earth's atmospheric composition has changed from the formation of the Earth through current time.

B7477CF0DFE601316F1168A86D17958E.description: Explain how heat and energy transfer in and out of the atmosphere; and provide examples of how it is related to weather and climate.

B74710E0DFE601316F1068A86D17958E.description: Explain how winds and ocean currents are created on the Earth's surface.

B7463CF0DFE601316F0E68A86D17958E.description: The Earth and Earth materials, as we know them today, have developed over long periods of time, through constant change processes.

B74573C0DFE601316F0C68A86D17958E.description: Collaborate with interested learners using appropriate web resources and publication media such as journals (print and electronic).

B744A820DFE601316F0A68A86D17958E.description: Use science learned to create a personal action plan on a community issue.

B7444EA0DFE601316F0968A86D17958E.description: Identify the reputable and appropriate communities of learners to whom research findings should be reported, compare data, and adapt as needed.

B74394A0DFE601316F0768A86D17958E.description: Self-assess progress toward a predetermined outcome and decide what needs to be done to meet the goal.

B7433690DFE601316F0668A86D17958E.description: Use key ideas of science to document and explain through an investigation the relationship between science and concepts.

B74289C0DFE601316F0468A86D17958E.description: Collect, synthesize, and report information from a variety of points of view.

B7422930DFE601316F0368A86D17958E.description: Create a culminating team project that demonstrates content knowledge and conceptual understanding and shows connections between science content and real-world settings.

B7415F50DFE601316F0168A86D17958E.description: Model solutions to a range of problems in science and technology using computer simulation software.

B74107D0DFE601316F0068A86D17958E.description: Use electronic networks to share information.

B740ADE0DFE601316EFF68A86D17958E.description: Prepare multimedia presentations to share results of investigations, demonstrating a clear sense of audience and purpose.

B73FEF80DFE601316EFD68A86D17958E.description: Develop models and explanations to fit evidence obtained through investigations.

B73976B0DFE601316EFC68A86D17958E.description: Plan and conduct practical tests to solve problems or answer a question, collect and analyze data using appropriate instruments and techniques safely and accurately.

B7391930DFE601316EFB68A86D17958E.description: Formulate scientific questions about an issue and define experimental procedures for finding answers.

B7385290DFE601316EF968A86D17958E.description: Apply scientific knowledge and skills to make reasoned decisions about the use of science and scientific innovations.

B737E6C0DFE601316EF868A86D17958E.description: Generate solutions to scientific questions and challenges through developing, modeling and revising investigations.

B7377C30DFE601316EF768A86D17958E.description: Pursue scientific inquiry such as observation, measurement, hypothesis formation and analysis, and value "habits of mind" such as persistence, accuracy, and collaboration.

B7368E20DFE601316EF568A86D17958E.description: Create a multimedia presentation incorporating numeric symbolic and/or graphic modes of representation to share scientific ideas, plans, results, and conclusions.

B73610F0DFE601316EF468A86D17958E.description: Create written reports and journals to share and communicate scientific ideas, plans, results, and conclusions resulting from observations and investigations.

B735B720DFE601316EF368A86D17958E.description: Select and use appropriate scientific vocabulary to orally share and communicate scientific ideas, plans, results, and conclusions resulting from investigations.

B734FB00DFE601316EF168A86D17958E.description: Analyze data and information gathered to clarify problems or issues identifying costs and benefits from a social, cultural, and/or environmental perspective; predict the consequences of action or inaction; and propose possible solutions.

B7348EB0DFE601316EF068A86D17958E.description: Collect and use qualitative and quantitative data and information, seek evidence and sources of information to identify flaws such as errors and bias, and explain how the evidence supports or refutes an initial hypothesis.

B7343280DFE601316EEF68A86D17958E.description: Select and analyze information from various sources (including electronic resources, print resources, community resources) and personally collected data to answer questions being investigated.

B7281710DFE601316ED068A86D17958E.description: Recognize that things can change in detail, but remain the same in general (e.g., the players change but the team remains, the cells are replaced but the organism remains); sometimes counterbalancing changes are necessary for a thing to retain its essential constancy in the presence of changing conditions.

B7273530DFE601316ECE68A86D17958E.description: Understand that the basic idea of mathematical modeling is to find a mathematical relationship that behaves in the same way as the objects or processes under investigation; a mathematical model may give insight about how something really works or may fit observations very well without any intuitive meaning.

B7263E30DFE601316ECC68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate that even in some very simple systems, it may not always be possible to predict accurately the result of changing some part or connection.

B725C7E0DFE601316ECB68A86D17958E.description: Give examples to show that a system usually has some properties that are different from those of its parts, but appear because of the interaction of those parts.

B72549D0DFE601316ECA68A86D17958E.description: Realize that systems may be so closely related that there is no way to draw boundaries that separate all parts of one from all parts of the others.

B72490A0DFE601316EC868A86D17958E.description: Realize that in science, the testing, revising, and occasional discarding of theories, new and old, never ends; this ongoing process leads to an increasingly better understanding of how things work in the world but not to absolute truth.

B72436C0DFE601316EC768A86D17958E.description: Show how the usefulness of a model can be tested by comparing its predictions to actual observations in the real world; but a close match does not mean that the model is the only "true" model or the one that would work.

B723D960DFE601316EC668A86D17958E.description: Understand that in the long run, theories are judged by how they fit with other theories, the range of observations they explain, how well they explain observations, and how effective they are in predicting new findings.

B7237760DFE601316EC568A86D17958E.description: Show how hypotheses are widely used in science for choosing what data to pay attention to and what additional data to seek, and for guiding the interpretation of the data (both new and previously available).

B7231FB0DFE601316EC468A86D17958E.description: Recognize that sometimes scientists can control conditions in order to focus on the effect of a single variable; when that is not possible for practical or ethical reasons, they try to observe as wide a range of natural occurrences as possible to be able to discern patterns.

B722C6D0DFE601316EC368A86D17958E.description: Test how well a theory predicts a phenomena.

B7226DC0DFE601316EC268A86D17958E.description: Explore new phenomena through investigations conducted for different reasons, or to check on previous results.

B7214AE0DFE601316EBF68A86D17958E.description: Provide a statement that addresses and answers the question investigated in light of the evidence generated in the investigation.

B720DC60DFE601316EBE68A86D17958E.description: Explain how data support or refute the hypothesis or prediction.

B7201030DFE601316EBC68A86D17958E.description: Compile and display data, evidence and information by hand and computer, in a variety of formats, including diagrams, flow charts, tables, graphs and scatter plots.

B71FAC00DFE601316EBB68A86D17958E.description: Representing and Understanding Results of Investigations

B71F4DF0DFE601316EBA68A86D17958E.description: Compile and organize data, using appropriate units.

B71EF530DFE601316EB968A86D17958E.description: Use instruments effectively and accurately for collecting data.

B71E9DB0DFE601316EB868A86D17958E.description: Select and use apparatus and material safely.

B71DD7D0DFE601316EB668A86D17958E.description: State a hypothesis and prediction based on available evidence and background information.

B71D7E60DFE601316EB568A86D17958E.description: Apply scientific theories and laws to new situations to generate hypotheses.

B71CCEA0DFE601316EB368A86D17958E.description: Identify limitations of a given classification system and identify alternative ways of classifying to accommodate anomalies.

B71C7390DFE601316EB268A86D17958E.description: Evaluate complex methods of classification for a specific purpose.

B71C1200DFE601316EB168A86D17958E.description: Use complex classification criteria and keys to identify items/organisms.

B71BB100DFE601316EB068A86D17958E.description: Ask questions about relationships among variables that can be observed directly as well as those that cannot.

9E2422C66EF4457BAC22F45434E15C8A.description: Develop a model to describe that matter is made of particles too small to be seen.

document.title: NH Career & College-Ready Science Standards (NGSS)

7221338D34A443D9A4A172A56CC46326.description: Develop a model to generate data for iterative testing and modification of a proposed object, tool, or process such that an optimal design can be achieved.

0DF8D2257A00447295AB31491025EBDA.description: Analyze data from tests to determine similarities and differences among several design solutions to identify the best characteristics of each that can be combined into a new solution to better meet the criteria for success.

F08C6922DF514B999E99B36FBF310F93.description: Evaluate competing design solutions using a systematic process to determine how well they meet the criteria and constraints of the problem.

CB00E9481FD84DB29B5C0780DFB3A423.description: Define the criteria and constraints of a design problem with sufficient precision to ensure a successful solution, taking into account relevant scientific principles and potential impacts on people and the natural environment that may limit possible solutions.

DE545AFD2EB44F309A6DC33BA26D7CB9.description: Ask questions to clarify evidence of the factors that have caused the rise in global temperatures over the past century.

32B05741C2774C3AB41799050DFBFC73.description: Construct an argument supported by evidence for how increases in human population and per-capita consumption of natural resources impact Earth's systems.

A439754F546E4892868B2FEBBFB49079.description: Apply scientific principles to design a method for monitoring and minimizing a human impact on the environment.

30F0142CA99A46B591680EEDBF7D0BD9.description: Analyze and interpret data on natural hazards to forecast future catastrophic events and inform the development of technologies to mitigate their effects.

5D06D522C8F64F22910938F14EAA45FD.description: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for how the uneven distributions of Earth's mineral, energy, and groundwater resources are the result of past and current geoscience processes.

61ADE473E32443158C210B65F3B91850.description: Collect data to provide evidence for how the motions and complex interactions of air masses results in changes in weather conditions.

F0FE0D9B74E845DFB33A1A9C1916252E.description: Develop a model to describe the cycling of water through Earth's systems driven by energy from the sun and the force of gravity.

041D6EAA09E048A7869A94654E0C3D24.description: Analyze and interpret data on the distribution of fossils and rocks, continental shapes, and seafloor structures to provide evidence of the past plate motions.

92A0BD81CE734553876CE1450DF5C54F.description: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how geoscience processes have changed Earth's surface at varying time and spatial scales.

3D54998BEF5E47FE8CF8F09BC4BF02F4.description: Develop a model to describe the cycling of Earth's materials and the flow of energy that drives this process.

A02DF4AC3F65494FAB6EFC8EB994740B.description: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence from rock strata for how the geologic time scale is used to organize Earth's 4.6-billion-year-old history.

15C566195D664B7CAED9C1A666BC59F1.description: Analyze and interpret data to determine scale properties of objects in the solar system.

B335F3DA7D0648CB8083CA10CD89F6CF.description: Develop and use a model to describe the role of gravity in the motions within galaxies and the solar system.

151B8A2E250C472483E413E708B58CB2.description: Develop and use a model of the Earth-sun-moon system to describe the cyclic patterns of lunar phases, eclipses of the sun and moon, and seasons.

726F519D2E014D3798EDDEF99B8DCD0E.description: Use mathematical representations to support explanations of how natural selection may lead to increases and decreases of specific traits in populations over time.

373FC9EF710D47B3895340DA05818551.description: Gather and synthesize information about the technologies that have changed the way humans influence the inheritance of desired traits in organisms.

9637A05F1D2F45F799AA8F85D9EE2BA2.description: Construct an explanation based on evidence that describes how genetic variations of traits in a population increase some individuals' probability of surviving and reproducing in a specific environment.

A73C9C5855804ADA8852ABEA9402BC62.description: Analyze displays of pictorial data to compare patterns of similarities in the embryological development across multiple species to identify relationships not evident in the fully formed anatomy.

7810EB79616147A0BA95DFFA185362E4.description: Apply scientific ideas to construct an explanation for the anatomical similarities and differences among modern organisms and between modern and fossil organisms to infer evolutionary relationships.

471E8E5E41C343289CF3C2B8F3BDC9AC.description: Analyze and interpret data for patterns in the fossil record that document the existence, diversity, extinction, and change of life forms throughout the history of life on Earth under the assumption that natural laws operate today as in the past.

7B503B99FC0D43F99B74DB76938B74CD.description: Develop and use a model to describe why asexual reproduction results in offspring with identical genetic information and sexual reproduction results in offspring with genetic variation.

46E52E06F1C1437DB76358670B9F8020.description: Develop and use a model to describe why structural changes to genes (mutations) located on chromosomes may affect proteins and may result in harmful, beneficial, or neutral effects to the structure and function of the organism.

9315A16E14A943C49B810E3A9623AFEE.description: Evaluate competing design solutions for maintaining biodiversity and ecosystem services.

B70E32F275F94EBCBDC1E583FACD3FB9.description: Construct an argument supported by empirical evidence that changes to physical or biological components of an ecosystem affect populations.

12DBD8FBB0D04FF0BEACF53F91B5EFC5.description: Develop a model to describe the cycling of matter and flow of energy among living and nonliving parts of an ecosystem.

A4FF608A8C87417B85D7DC80A053DE0B.description: Construct an explanation that predicts patterns of interactions among organisms across multiple ecosystems.

023A5BA6A4AF4C95991B4633ECC6818B.description: Analyze and interpret data to provide evidence for the effects of resource availability on organisms and populations of organisms in an ecosystem.

B863D3EC22D64A40A0A082A6AAA5F087.description: Gather and synthesize information that sensory receptors respond to stimuli by sending messages to the brain for immediate behavior or storage as memories.

930CCA5F11FF469899F35C9A6775E355.description: Develop a model to describe how food is rearranged through chemical reactions forming new molecules that support growth and/or release energy as this matter moves through an organism.

0D7BDD2CED0E463DB50CB3017363E1CD.description: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for the role of photosynthesis in the cycling of matter and flow of energy into and out of organisms.

792B2D4B157B4D3A8EF119B0889EBBDA.description: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for how environmental and genetic factors influence the growth of organisms.

6BDC0177D7C947F9B42ADE1180DD526F.description: Use argument based on empirical evidence and scientific reasoning to support an explanation for how characteristic animal behaviors and specialized plant structures affect the probability of successful reproduction of animals and plants respectively.

80C8B7C8495E40A88F3E078159AA4560.description: Use argument supported by evidence for how the body is a system of interacting subsystems composed of groups of cells.

504C9D223AF9436AB420E199372A0984.description: Develop and use a model to describe the function of a cell as a whole and ways parts of cells contribute to the function.

445E54C3AB804103BF3D27DA897054FD.description: Conduct an investigation to provide evidence that living things are made of cells; either one cell or many different numbers and types of cells.

64D98C9F93664FCF80A4A70638767396.description: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

2D1C676488F742B69DAD41052795089B.description: Integrate qualitative scientific and technical information to support the claim that digitized signals are a more reliable way to encode and transmit information than analog signals.

1FE7773219A640E184DE2F665BC3E7A9.description: Develop and use a model to describe that waves are reflected, absorbed, or transmitted through various materials.

DF929BFCA76743BCACE7183358A3F6A1.description: Use mathematical representations to describe a simple model for waves that includes how the amplitude of a wave is related to the energy in a wave.

F672C2D08AA04D968AF4DDEE361C0160.description: Waves and Their Applications in Technologies for Information Transfer

C49076F10BE645B5B0007C63FC06DEE9.description: Construct, use, and present arguments to support the claim that when the kinetic energy of an object changes, energy is transferred to or from the object.

BC359A3537DB4BE7928FE2340112E743.description: Plan an investigation to determine the relationships among the energy transferred, the type of matter, the mass, and the change in the average kinetic energy of the particles as measured by the temperature of the sample.

DAD42206FF1340FC9A62E00B189EE955.description: Apply scientific principles to design, construct, and test a device that either minimizes or maximizes thermal energy transfer.

71148064349D4591A27B69104AB21A79.description: Develop a model to describe that when the arrangement of objects interacting at a distance changes, different amounts of potential energy are stored in the system.

40630828C1834F7B94A0F6F913260CD4.description: Construct and interpret graphical displays of data to describe the relationships of kinetic energy to the mass of an object and to the speed of an object.

E5410255D1D14C0FAAF1986C46B1EBC0.description: Conduct an investigation and evaluate the experimental design to provide evidence that fields exist between objects exerting forces on each other even though the objects are not in contact.

F8CEDE49865D4B8CA04A84A91B795140.description: Construct and present arguments using evidence to support the claim that gravitational interactions are attractive and depend on the masses of interacting objects.

FEA8CECE5DA64459BF69F0A92EBB66D2.description: Ask questions about data to determine the factors that affect the strength of electric and magnetic forces.

67F27CA68AEB4C07BB018A552E2A3857.description: Plan an investigation to provide evidence that the change in an object's motion depends on the sum of the forces on the object and the mass of the object.

A63EA459578A4A6DA8A46C9EEBE3359F.description: Apply Newton's Third Law to design a solution to a problem involving the motion of two colliding objects.

3B30FD4F9B394A9C8B07C03338F40451.description: Develop a model that predicts and describes changes in particle motion, temperature, and state of a pure substance when thermal energy is added or removed.

E355CBEB3FA24F1283729FD4B1F4B146.description: Analyze and interpret data on the properties of substances before and after the substances interact to determine if a chemical reaction has occurred.

3EE1C7CAE4C74A7C8395A4D8AE651897.description: Develop models to describe the atomic composition of simple molecules and extended structures.

6F247CBD23004BCEB8419D50FA2F8BD3.description: Transfer knowledge and skills with various software techniques to finish media productions.

document.title: NH Early Learning Standards

C10F0EAEF27140F9A5A480C5AFFD9CBF.description: Four- and Five-Year-Olds: Increasingly use words instead of actions to express their emotions

ED5EFC122FDE4E1B9C975033C2F35B1C.description: Four- and Five-Year-Olds: May still have difficulty regulating strong emotions

7A6702F054C44D47A11DC3DFF9B1D8DA.description:
Three Years: Begin to respond to an adult’s
cues about regulating their
emotions (E.g. At drop-off
time, Sage begins to control
his crying when his teacher
says, “I know you’re sad,
would you like to see what
your friends are doing?”)

30B65A8CF38F4D3E9678545F13837DAC.description:
Thirty Months to
Three Years: Begin using words to describe
their feelings while still
expressing strong emotions

25221DF6FF4E4C77A2EFEF71CEBFFC0B.description:
Twenty-Four to
Thirty Months: Have difficulty regulating strong
feelings

76CD4337BB7C4DF38929EE456A0B861E.description:
Eighteen to
Twenty-Four Months: Use comfort objects or certain
behaviors to calm themselves
(E.g. Finn finds and holds his
blanket to calm himself.)

4F1F8FA8D8E34258A4083BDE5144DD22.description:
Nine Months to
Eighteen Months
: Follow their caregiver to keep
him/her in sight

498C6B5D478A4057B5D53F6A96E4E58A.description:
Birth to
Nine Months: By 9 months, stop crying when
their needs are met or they
expect their needs to be met

9B60763BD00D4C60B4EAADC8DB6576A1.description: Four- and Five-Year-Olds: Explore emotions in various ways (through play, art, music, and dance)

ADE6B8F0AE99497D896DB1093722EA58.description:
Four- and Five-Year-Olds: Demonstrate increasing competencies in recognizing and describing their own
emotions

21DB4ED01667458CAEE5BD2C553EB468.description:
Three Years: Express their feelings verbally
with greater frequency

FCE791047B784B8CBCE8B1A6D9630B17.description:
Thirty Months to
Three Years: Verbally relate their needs,
wants, and feelings to others

E16D7A74AEFD46C898C23538B0F7C585.description:
Twenty-Four to
Thirty Months: Share their feelings through
talking and pretend play

54A5108727824FBC92F2574F052DA027.description:
Eighteen to
Twenty-Four Months: May express their feelings
strongly including extended
episodes and may not be easily
distracted

DE9436C4C235471083475F5C89448DC6.description:
Nine Months to
Eighteen Months
: Begin to express a variety of
feelings through vocalizations,
facial expressions, and body
movements

65324E2ACB13469E921F8388F12451C3.description:
Birth to
Nine Months: Express enjoyment and
unhappiness in their
environment

7F70DE9AF35D434580FF6C697B6CE426.description:
Four- and Five-Year-Olds: Begin to be able to stop undesirable behaviors on their own or with a gentle
reminder (E.g. Xavier starts to grab Zach’s car, but stops himself and asks, “Can
I use that when you’re done?”)

EA9B95A3A048494CB2D3F32A17F2D2C9.description:
Three Years: Follow classroom rules and
routines with guidance

E2A75D98005F4492A3E97525254597F0.description:
Thirty Months to
Three Years: Show increased self-regulation
and awareness of how their
actions affect others

AA92FF97FCBF41A9B005F523232DBE37.description:
Twenty-Four to
Thirty Months: With adult guidance, can begin to
tone down aggressive behaviors.

9AFDEB15176A4370964EC9AF8A0E2791.description:
Eighteen to
Twenty-Four Months: With guidance, demonstrate
they can use some classroom
materials appropriately (E.g.
The teacher shows her toddlers
how to handle books gently and
Clara turns the pages carefully.)

3D051A7A9C364BE69924119D991AD1A0.description:
Nine Months to
Eighteen Months
: Need adult support to regulate
physical expressions of emotions
(E.g. Marigold pulls another
baby’s hair until the teacher
takes her hand and shows her
how to pat the baby gently.)

AFA649328458434CB96A7FBF293C0BD9.description:
Birth to
Nine Months: Calm themselves (E.g.
9-month-old Vinod babbles in
his crib until his father comes
to get him up from his nap.)

7EDAFCD6BF7F4E25A15AADF9DE518016.description:
Four- and Five-Year-Olds:  Begin to understand the reasons for others’ emotions and respond appropriately
(E.g. Audrey says to a friend who is upset over not getting the toy she wanted
during play, “You’ll get to play with it next time.”)

E4BC47AD5AE148C6AF078C6F76CDF6BD.description:
Three Years: Begin to label others’ feelings
and recognize reasons for
those feelings

B39B736B931E41C092DCDFB3485490A3.description:
Thirty Months to
Three Years: Begin to display empathy
towards other children

25FA4022F6CD46A580723D822629F9E0.description:
Twenty-Four to
Thirty Months: May try to comfort children who
are distressed (E.g. Filomena
gives her teddy bear to Ellen,
who is crying.)

91DE5F23DDBD45E0B81970CF3FD2DBBE.description:
Eighteen to
Twenty-Four Months: Demonstrate interest in the
feelings of another child

ABD23CAFF3D84FEC8EBA636FD69DFB0A.description:
Nine Months to
Eighteen Months
: Show awareness in other
people’s emotions

09D5DA7239194DEFB0BB085481D4FBE0.description:
Birth to
Nine Months: May cry when another baby
cries

C8B5D9B4253540E2847F1A5A436432A5.description:
Four- and Five-Year-Olds: Develop friendships, sometimes based on shared interests or
characteristics

522378663B0249D8A642DDD6D62A04BD.description:
Four- and Five-Year-Olds: Sustain interaction by cooperating, helping, sharing, and expressing interest,
though they may need adult guidance

4A030CB96E644226B5938EF7B626F76B.description:
Four- and Five-Year-Olds: Build skills needed to participate successfully as a member of a group, such as
taking turns

AF39D105ADEC4FF799FCA435387CCBFB.description: Four- and Five-Year-Olds: Approach others with expectations of positive interactions

691CAF8BFAA6437FA9E1B505B53A0F7F.description:
Three Years: Play cooperatively with other
children and show preference
for some children over
others (E.g. Jose and Chris
are playing together. When
Martin comes over, Chris says,
“No, go away.”)

7258148E0DD64EF980E1ED5739ECB2B2.description:
Thirty Months to
Three Years: Begin to play cooperatively for
brief periods with other children

3CB10C7BCBD04DEFB8BD82256E8E9144.description:
Twenty-Four to
Thirty Months: Engage in brief or momentary
interactions with other children,
but may need adult support
(E.g. Siddarth yells, “Run, run,”
to several other children on the
playground.)

867FF20C3DD34F3E86B29279A58151CD.description:
Eighteen to
Twenty-Four Months: Play alongside other children,
with or without acknowledging
their presence

745C10423EA1498C8C87594B937C0E02.description:
Nine Months to
